items.en: Finely chopped pork (the shop calls the cut a secret), collagen-rich, topped with mizuna and spring onion and eaten dressed in ponzu — the card compares the texture to shredded fugu skin
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: The card's own description says to dress it in ポン酢 — ponzu is built on soy sauce, which is wheat, so this is a wheat dish unless the shop names a gluten-free version. Two prices are printed, ¥800 and ¥900, the ¥900 one marked ザラメコラーゲン入り on the card.

items.en: Thin-sliced 'teppo' (the thick part of the large intestine) tossed with cucumber and the shop's own spicy meat-miso
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: 自家製辛肉みそ — a house meat-miso. Miso is a gluten question in itself (麦味噌 is barley) and Japanese chilli-meat miso is normally loosened with soy sauce or mirin; the meat also rules out vegan.

items.en: Slowly, gently cooked pork belly served like raw ham, eaten with wasabi soy sauce
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: The card itself says 「わさび醤油でお召し上がりください」 — soy sauce, i.e. wheat.

items.en: Slow-cooked pork jowl ('buta-toro') dressed simply with spring onion, salt and sesame oil
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: The card names only ネギ・塩・ごま油 — spring onion, salt and sesame oil, with no soy sauce mentioned, which makes this one of the more promising plates here. Not confirmed by any allergen statement, and the kitchen has soy sauce everywhere, so ask.

items.en: Pork-heart salad — thin-sliced heart mixed through vegetables in a balsamic-vinegar-and-vinegared-miso dressing
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: The dressing is バルサミコ酢 + 酢みそ per the card. Miso is the gluten question (麦味噌 is barley) and vinegared-miso dressings commonly carry dashi as well.

items.en: Pork-intestine salad — the same dressing as はつサラ, made with shiro
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: Card says 「はつサラと同じドレッシングで、シロバージョンです」 — same 酢みそ dressing, same barley-miso question.

items.en: Poached tongue steeped in a yuzu-soy-based marinade, finished with salt, pepper and basil
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: The card says the marinade is 柚しょうゆベースのタレ — soy sauce, i.e. wheat.

items.en: Blanched pork liver with spring onion and ponzu
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: Card says ポン酢 — soy-sauce based, wheat.

items.en: Tonkimo again with grated garlic and ginger added, tataki-style
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: Built on とんきも, which the card serves with ポン酢 (soy sauce, wheat).

items.en: Tongue braised in plenty of red wine, served under a shallot sauce
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: Wine-braised, with an エシャロットソース. Neither the wine nor the sauce is specified; a Western-style sauce may be flour-thickened and Japanese kitchens often add soy sauce to a braise. Ask.

items.en: Throat-cut pork poached and thinly sliced, eaten with ponzu
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: Card says ポン酢 — soy sauce, wheat.

items.en: Thin-sliced heart blanched and shocked in iced water, with spring onion and momiji-oroshi, dressed in ponzu
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: Card says ポン酢 — soy sauce, wheat.

items.en: Liver eaten with salt and olive oil
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: The card names only 塩 and オリーブオイル — no soy sauce in the description. That makes it one of the better candidates on this menu, but there is no allergen statement anywhere in the shop and the liver is cooked in a kitchen that uses soy sauce on almost everything else. Ask.

items.en: 'Fourth-block liver' — liver under a fruity tare with vegetables
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: The card says フルーティーなタレ. An izakaya タレ is soy-sauce based unless stated otherwise.

items.en: Rare liver with cheese, salt, white sesame and apricot, combined as you like
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: Card lists チーズ、塩、白ゴマ、アンズ — no soy sauce named. Dairy rules out vegan; the gluten question is only whether anything is added at the pass, so ask.

items.en: Wind-dried liver ('liver jerky') dressed with gagome kombu — the card calls it a delicacy
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: がごめ昆布 is kelp, which is neither wheat nor animal, but dried/cured offal is very often cured with soy sauce and the card does not say. Ask.

items.ja: 風干しレバーのサラダ
items.en: The wind-dried liver built into a salad
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: Same liver as above; the salad dressing is not named on the card, and dressings are the usual hiding place for soy sauce.

items.en: Seared red-chicken thigh and breast, eaten with ponzu or ginger soy sauce
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: The card offers ポンズ or 生姜じょうゆ — both are soy sauce, i.e. wheat.

items.en: Pork belly seared over charcoal, laid on shredded cabbage
items.section: 喜美松オリジナルメニュー Kimimatsu original dishes
items.note: The card describes only the charcoal searing and the cabbage — no sauce is named, which is unusual and worth asking about, because charcoal grills here are shared with tare-basted skewers.

items.en: House potato salad
items.note: Japanese potato salad is bound with mayonnaise, so egg rules out vegan. Mayonnaise is not usually a wheat ingredient but the shop publishes nothing; ask.

items.en: Cherry tomatoes
items.note: A plain vegetable plate as printed. Nothing on the card says whether it arrives dressed, and this kitchen's default dressings are ponzu and 酢みそ. Ask and it may be your cleanest option here.

items.en: Young shallots, eaten raw
items.note: Raw エシャレット is served in izakaya with miso to dip. Miso is the gluten question (麦味噌 is barley) and may carry dashi. The shallots themselves are plain.

items.en: Vegetables dressed with Japanese mustard
items.note: からし和え is mustard loosened with soy sauce and usually dashi — wheat from the soy sauce. The dashi is also the vegan question.

items.en: Vegetables dressed with ground sesame
items.note: ゴマ和え is ground sesame, sugar and soy sauce — wheat by default. Dashi is often in it too, which is the vegan question as well as a second soy-sauce route.

items.en: Vegetables under vinegared miso
items.note: 酢味噌 — miso, which may be 麦味噌 (barley), and vinegared-miso dressings frequently include dashi.

items.en: A plate of boiled vegetables
items.note: Plain boiled vegetables, but the card does not say what they are served with; this kitchen's standard dips are miso and ponzu. Ask for it plain with salt.

items.en: Baked potato with butter
items.note: Butter rules out vegan. Potato and butter carry no wheat ingredient, but there is no allergen statement and the potato may be shared with the fryer plates. Ask.

items.en: Grilled garlic
items.note: Grilled on the same charcoal as the tare-basted offal skewers — see the yakimono note. Seasoning not stated.

items.en: Boiled bean sprouts
items.note: Boiled sprouts are plain in themselves; the dressing is not printed, and this kitchen dresses with ponzu and miso by default.

items.en: Chilled tofu
items.note: Hiyayakko is served with soy sauce (wheat) and is topped with katsuobushi in most izakaya, which is the vegan problem. Ask for it undressed and it becomes a different question.

items.en: Tofu under ground sesame
items.note: The sesame topping is normally loosened with soy sauce; tofu itself is plant-based.

items.en: Offal simmered slowly — the Tokyo motsu-yaki standard
items.note: モツ煮込み is simmered in miso and/or soy sauce; both are gluten routes (barley miso, wheat soy sauce). Offal rules out vegan.

items.en: Pork and vegetable miso soup
items.note: Miso plus dashi plus pork. Miso may be 麦味噌 (barley); dashi in a Japanese kitchen is normally 白だし or だし醤油, which are soy-sauce based, i.e. wheat — and bonito, which is the vegan problem.

items.en: Fried aubergine
items.note: Deep-fried. Japanese fried aubergine is normally dusted with flour or starch, and the fryer is shared with the croquettes, which are panko-breaded — cross-contamination either way.

items.en: Aubergine with meat-miso
items.note: Meat-miso: pork (not vegan) plus miso, which may be barley, usually let down with soy sauce.

items.en: Grilled aubergine
items.note: Grilled aubergine is traditionally served with ginger and soy sauce, and this grill is shared with tare-basted skewers. The card names no sauce. Ask.

items.en: Fried potato
items.note: Shared fryer with the panko-breaded コロッケ.

items.en: Crisps / potato chips
items.note: Not stated whether these are fried in-house (shared fryer) or a bought-in bag; that changes the answer completely.

items.en: Croquette, one piece
items.note: Croquettes are breaded in パン粉 (wheat breadcrumbs) and normally bound with a flour batter; the standard filling is potato with minced beef or pork.

items.en: Rice-bran pickles
items.note: ぬか漬 is pickled in a rice-bran bed — rice bran itself is not a gluten grain, but nukadoko is often started with beer or barley and pickles are frequently finished with soy sauce. Ask.

items.en: Kimchi
items.note: Commercial kimchi in Japan usually contains 魚醤 or salted shrimp (the vegan problem) and sometimes wheat starch or soy sauce in the seasoning paste. The shop does not say whose kimchi it is.

items.en: Grilled fried tofu skin
items.note: Abura-age is grilled and served with soy sauce and often katsuobushi; the tofu itself is plant-based, the topping is where both problems live.

items.en: Tongue root simmered with ginger
items.note: 生姜煮 is a soy-sauce-and-ginger braise — wheat by default.

items.en: Simmered ganmodoki (deep-fried tofu fritter)
items.note: 煮もの is simmered in dashi and soy sauce — wheat. The dashi is also the vegan question; ganmodoki itself often contains egg or yam as a binder.

items.ja: 里イモとイカの煮もの
items.en: Taro and squid simmered together
items.note: PRICE NOT RECORDED — the figure runs off the edge of the menu photograph; only 「¥70…」 is legible, so it is not written here rather than guessed. Simmered in dashi and soy sauce (wheat); squid rules out vegan.

items.en: The compulsory seat appetiser — contents change
items.note: PRICE NOT RECORDED — the figure is cut off at the bottom of the menu photograph (legible as 「¥40…」). You do not choose an otōshi and it is not described anywhere, so it is the one plate on this menu a coeliac or vegan diner should decline or query at the moment of sitting down.

items.ja: （メニュー1品、テープで隠されています）
items.en: One line on the small-plates card has been taped over by the shop; the price ¥500 is still visible
items.note: Recorded only so the reader is not surprised by an untranslatable line on the card. The dish name is physically covered with tape in the menu photograph, so it is not named here. Vegan status was left blank by an earlier pass and is not established by any source read; recorded as ask. Gluten status was left blank by an earlier pass and is not established by any source read; recorded as ask.

items.en: Offal hot pot, per person
items.section: お鍋 Nabe — hot pots (orders taken until 21:00; every pot available from one portion)
items.note: The card gives no broth base. Motsu-nabe broth is soy-sauce or miso, both gluten routes, and it is built on offal and usually a bonito/pork stock. The shop's card states 「お鍋の御注文は21時までにお願いします」.

items.en: Minced-meat-ball hot pot, per person
items.section: お鍋 Nabe — hot pots (orders taken until 21:00; every pot available from one portion)
items.note: Same broth question as もつ鍋, plus the tsukune binder (wheat flour or breadcrumb is the Japanese default).

items.en: Extra hot-pot filling — offal or tsukune, each
items.section: お鍋 Nabe — hot pots (orders taken until 21:00; every pot available from one portion)
items.note: Goes into the same unnamed broth.

items.ja: 具の追加：ニラ／キャベツ／もやし／油あげ／ネギ／えのき／ナス
items.en: Extra hot-pot vegetables — garlic chives, cabbage, bean sprouts, fried tofu skin, spring onion, enoki mushrooms or aubergine, each
items.section: お鍋 Nabe — hot pots (orders taken until 21:00; every pot available from one portion)
items.note: The vegetables themselves are plant-based, but they are cooked in the shared offal broth, whose base the card does not name — that is both the gluten and the vegan problem.

items.en: Offal shabu-shabu, per person — the first offal comes as a chef's-choice three-piece plate
items.section: お鍋 Nabe — hot pots (orders taken until 21:00; every pot available from one portion)
items.note: Card: 「最初のもつはおまかせ3点盛りになります」. Shabu-shabu is eaten with ポン酢 or ごまだれ, both soy-sauce based, and the broth base is not named.

items.ja: もつ各（レバ／がつ／タン／シロ／はつ／コブクロ）
items.en: Extra shabu-shabu offal — liver, stomach, tongue, shiro, heart or uterus, each
items.section: お鍋 Nabe — hot pots (orders taken until 21:00; every pot available from one portion)
items.note: As above.

items.en: Vegetable plate for the hot pot
items.section: お鍋 Nabe — hot pots (orders taken until 21:00; every pot available from one portion)
items.note: Plant ingredients cooked in the shared offal broth.

items.en: To finish the pot: rice porridge cooked in the remaining broth, per person
items.section: お鍋 Nabe — hot pots (orders taken until 21:00; every pot available from one portion)
items.note: Rice itself is gluten-free, but ojiya is made in the used hot-pot broth, and beaten egg is standard.

items.en: To finish the pot: ramen noodles in the remaining broth, per person
items.section: お鍋 Nabe — hot pots (orders taken until 21:00; every pot available from one portion)
items.note: Ramen noodles are wheat, and they go into the used offal broth.

items.en: Rice ball with kombu
items.note: Kombu onigiri filling is 昆布の佃煮 — kelp simmered in soy sauce, i.e. wheat. Kelp itself is plant-based, but tsukudani sometimes carries dashi too.

items.en: Rice ball with bonito flakes
items.note: おかか is katsuobushi dressed with soy sauce — wheat, and fish.

items.en: Rice ball with pickled plum
items.note: Umeboshi is traditionally plum, salt and shiso, which would make this the cleanest rice ball on the card — but commercial umeboshi is often seasoned with dashi or 調味液 containing soy sauce. Ask which they use.

items.ja: 焼きおにぎり（しょうゆ）
items.en: Grilled rice ball, soy-glazed — the card labels it (しょうゆ)
items.note: The card itself names しょうゆ — soy sauce, wheat.

items.en: Plain steamed white rice
items.note: Plain steamed white rice is rice and water — no wheat and no animal ingredient, and it is the one thing on this menu a coeliac can rely on. The remaining risk is handling: order it plain (not 焼き, not 茶づけ, no sauce over it), and in a small motsu-yaki kitchen the scoop and the counter are shared. The shop publishes no allergen information at all, so say what you need.

items.en: Tsukune over rice with tea/broth poured on
items.note: 茶づけ broth is normally だし or だし醤油 (soy sauce, wheat; bonito, not vegan), and the tsukune binder is a second wheat question.

items.en: Ramen with tsukune
items.note: Ramen noodles are wheat, and ramen tare is soy sauce.

items.en: Cartilage curry
items.note: Japanese curry is thickened with a wheat-flour roux by default. The shop states nothing, so this is the assumption a coeliac has to make rather than a shop claim — but do not order it without confirmation.

items.en: Rice bowl topped with the grilled skewers of your choice
items.note: The card explains 「ごはんの上にお好きな焼きものをのせてお出しします（ごはん代＋焼きものの代）」 — the price is the rice plus whichever skewers you pick, from ¥500. The skewers carry the tare/soy-sauce question in the yakimono section.

items.en: Rice bowl topped with charcoal-seared pork belly
items.note: The あぶり豚バラ plate itself names no sauce, but a donburi is normally finished with a tare over the rice. Ask.

items.en: Rice bowl with the house pork and salad
items.note: Salad donburi means a dressing, and this kitchen's dressings are 酢みそ and ponzu — barley miso and wheat soy sauce respectively.

items.en: House warabimochi, made to order — the card warns it takes a little time
items.note: Warabimochi is bracken or potato starch, normally dusted with きな粉 (roasted soy flour) and poured with 黒蜜 — all three are wheat-free and plant-based in their standard forms, but the shop lists no ingredients and commercial kinako blends sometimes include barley flour. Ask.

items.en: Grilled banana
items.note: Grilled banana is normally finished with butter or honey (the vegan question), and this is a shop with one charcoal grill. Nothing is stated on the card.

items.en: Frozen banana
items.note: Frozen banana is often served chocolate-coated; the card says nothing beyond the name.

items.en: Draft beer, medium
items.note: 麦芽 — barley malt.

items.en: Draft beer, small
items.note: 麦芽 — barley malt.

items.ja: 瓶ビール（アサヒ大ビン）
items.en: Bottled beer, Asahi large bottle
items.note: Barley malt.

items.ja: 瓶ビール（キリン大ビン）
items.en: Bottled beer, Kirin large bottle
items.note: Barley malt.

items.ja: 瓶ビール（エビス中ビン）
items.en: Bottled beer, Yebisu medium bottle
items.note: Barley malt.

items.en: House mix of draft beer and fruit vinegar (ミチョ)
items.note: The card spells out the recipe: 生ビール＋ミチョ. Beer is barley malt.

items.en: Draft beer mixed with amazake
items.note: The card gives the recipe as 生ビール＋甘酒. Beer is barley malt; amazake is fermented rice kōji.

items.ja: ホッピー（焼酎＋ホッピー）
items.en: Hoppy — shochu with the malt beverage poured over (shochu ¥500, Hoppy ¥300)
items.note: Hoppy is a brewed malt beverage — barley. Never gluten-free, whatever the shochu base is.

items.en: Shochu with lemon
items.note: The base shochu is not named on this line, and this shop's shochu shelf includes 麦焼酎 (barley). Ask which bottle the sours are poured from.

items.en: Shochu with oolong tea
items.note: Oolong is tea leaf only, not 麦茶 — the question is only the base shochu, which is not named.

items.en: Shochu with green tea
items.note: Same unnamed base shochu.

items.en: Shochu with barley tea
items.note: 麦茶 is roasted BARLEY — a gluten grain, in the glass. This is the trap on the sour list.

items.en: Shochu with plum vinegar
items.note: Base shochu not named.

items.en: Sour shochu — the card offers a free apricot or grapefruit syrup (¥0) to sweeten it
items.note: Card: 「甘いシロップを入れられます／アンズ ¥0／グレープフルーツ ¥0」. Base shochu not named.

items.en: Shochu with shikuwasa (Okinawan citrus)
items.note: Base shochu not named.

items.ja: ウィスキーハイボール〈角〉
items.en: Suntory Kaku whisky highball
items.note: Whisky is distilled from barley malt.

items.ja: ウィスキーハイボール〈ニッカ フロンティア〉
items.en: Nikka Frontier whisky highball
items.note: Whisky — barley malt.

items.en: Jim Beam bourbon
items.note: Bourbon mash is mostly corn but includes malted barley.

items.en: Suntory Sui gin and soda
items.note: Gin is distilled, normally from a grain spirit; Suntory does not state the base grain on this card. Distillation removes gluten protein in practice, but that is not a shop claim.

items.en: Chestnut shochu, Dabada Hiburi — glass ¥700, bottle ¥3,900
items.note: Chestnut shochu is distilled with a rice-kōji starter; the card does not state the kōji grain.

items.en: Barley shochu, Gokuu — glass ¥700, bottle ¥3,900
items.note: 麦焼酎 is distilled from BARLEY. Not gluten-free on this app's rule.

items.en: Barley shochu, Muretsuru — glass ¥600, bottle ¥3,300
items.note: Barley shochu.

items.ja: 麦焼酎〈河童九千坊 本流〉
items.en: Barley shochu, Kappa Kusenbo Honryu — glass ¥600, bottle ¥3,300
items.note: Barley shochu.

items.en: Sweet-potato shochu, Kametsubo — glass ¥700, bottle ¥3,900

tokyo_monja_asakichi.price_note: Prices approximate — may change, and this record mixes TWO VINTAGES, deliberately. The もんじゃ section is transcribed from a photograph of the shop's own printed グランドメニュー taken 2026/04 and those figures are current. Everything else — okonomiyaki, teppanyaki, otsumami, rice, dessert, drinks — comes from the shop's own HotPepper page (もんじゃ浅吉 本店, strJ003365820, address 東京都台東区浅草2-14-11, matching the record), which is shop-maintained but was last updated 更新日 2022/09/19 (drinks 2022/09/20). THOSE OLDER PRICES ARE DEMONSTRABLY LOW: every monja that appears on both sources has risen since 2022 — ミックス ¥1,480→¥1,680, 明太もちチーズ ¥1,380→¥1,530, トマトチーズ ¥1,380→¥1,530, 豚キムチ ¥980→¥1,310, 辛ラーメン ¥1,080→¥1,350, 下町もんじゃ/下町天 ¥680→¥870. Read the 2022-sourced lines as roughly 15–25% below what you will be charged. Two monja on the 2022 page (鴨ねぎもんじゃ ¥1,380, シーチキンもんじゃ ¥880) do NOT appear on the 2026 card and are not listed here rather than being carried forward as if current. The Tabelog menu tab holds no registered items at all. The shop publishes NO allergen information anywhere — not on HotPepper, not on Instagram, not in the photographed card — so every gf/vegan flag is reasoning from the shop's own printed ingredient lists and from what monja unavoidably is, never a shop claim. In gluten terms this is one of the least survivable rooms in Tokyo: the batter is wheat, the griddle is the table, and every dish including the steaks and the fried rice is cooked in that batter's residue.

items.en: The house mixed monja — raw squid, sakura shrimp, dried shredded squid, corn, chikuwa fish cake, fish sausage, coarse pork, red pickled ginger, yakisoba noodles and tenkasu
items.note: The card prints the full filling list: 生いか・桜えび・きりいか・コーン・ちくわ・魚肉ソーセージ・豚粗・紅しょうが・そば・揚玉. Monja and okonomiyaki are a WHEAT-FLOUR batter cooked on the table griddle — there is no gluten-free version of this dish anywhere in this shop. The shop's own HotPepper copy adds a second wheat route: 「自家製の出汁で味付けされた生地」, the batter is seasoned with the house dashi, and a Japanese dashi is normally built on 白だし / めんつゆ / だし醤油, all soy-sauce based and therefore wheat. That dashi is also the vegan problem before you reach the egg and seafood. Note too that 「そば」 in a monja shop means Chinese-style WHEAT noodles (yakisoba), not buckwheat, and 揚玉 (tenkasu) is fried wheat batter. Marked おすすめ on the card.

tokyo_seabura_ramen_chaccha_te.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Transcribed from a photograph of the shop's OWN ticket machine (食券機) taken 2026/06, plus the shop's handwritten wall card for 飯 / トッピング / ドリンク from the same visit, which agrees with the machine on every overlapping line. There is no website and no registered Tabelog menu (the /dtlmenu/ URL falls through to the shop's top page), so the machine IS the menu. PRICES HAVE RISEN HARD: the same machine photographed 2025/02 read 背脂ラーメン ¥900 (now ¥980), チャーシューメン ¥1,280 (now ¥1,580), つけ麺 ¥1,100 (now ¥1,380), 味噌 ¥1,100 (now ¥1,280), ライス ¥280 (now ¥380). Anything you read about this shop older than 2026 is low. TWO BUTTONS ARE RECORDED WITHOUT A JAPANESE NAME (¥1,480 'Vegetable and Back-Fat Ramen', ¥1,380 'Spicy Miso Ramen'): the vertical Japanese names beside those two panels run off the edge of the 2026 frame, and no earlier photograph carries the same English captions, so they are left unnamed rather than invented. The five 限定 bowls come from the shop's pavement A-boards and carry no printed price. The shop publishes NO allergen information. This is a ramen shop: wheat noodles, a soy-sauce tare and pork back fat in every bowl. Nothing here is gluten-free and nothing is vegan except plain rice and the cola.

items.en: The original back-fat ramen — soy-sauce broth under a snowfall of pork back fat; the machine's English label reads Original Ramen
items.note: Ramen noodles are WHEAT — there is no gluten-free noodle here. The default 背脂ラーメン tare is 醤油 (soy sauce, brewed with wheat); the shop's own sign says it can be switched to 塩, which removes the soy-sauce tare from the seasoning but changes nothing about the noodles, and a shio tare is itself usually built on a soy-derived or wheat-containing stock. Everything in the bowl also sits in pork back-fat and a pork/chicken broth, so nothing on this menu is vegan either. The shop's counter sign states 「チャッチャ亭の背脂は、国産のAランク背脂のみを使用しています」 and lets you pick the quantity free of charge: 少チャッチャ (sweet and mild) / 並チャッチャ (rich) / 大チャッチャ (extra rich). The shop's sign above the machine reads 「背脂ラーメン（醤油）は塩味にも変更できます。※食券を渡す時にお伝えください」 — say so when you hand over the ticket.
