In a ramen shop this is the ONLY thing a coeliac can eat, and it is survival rather than a meal: keep it away from the tare bottle and the broth, and be aware the whole room is a wheat-noodle kitchen with a shared noodle boiler steaming over everything. The shop publishes no allergen information.

items.en: Half rice — sold as 追い飯, the rice you tip into what is left of your bowl
items.note: The rice itself is plain rice and nothing else. Note what it is FOR, though: 追い飯 means tipping it into the leftover tsukemen or mazesoba tare, which is soy sauce and pork. Eaten on its own it is clean; eaten as intended it is not.

items.en: Seasoned soft-boiled egg
items.note: Ajitama is marinated in a soy-sauce tare — wheat — and it is an egg.

items.en: Sheets of dried seaweed
items.note: Plain roasted nori is just seaweed, but ramen nori is often 味付け (seasoned with a soy-based liquid), and it is laid into a soy-and-pork broth the moment it arrives. Worth asking; not worth assuming.

items.ja: もやし or ワカメ
items.en: Bean sprouts, or wakame seaweed
items.note: Both are plant ingredients in themselves. In this shop they are blanched in and served on a pork broth, and ramen bean sprouts are commonly tossed with a stock seasoning.

items.en: Extra spring onion
items.note: Ramen negi topping is normally dressed in sesame oil with salt or a soy seasoning; the shop does not say which.

items.en: Fermented bamboo shoots
items.note: Menma is seasoned in a soy-sauce-based liquid, and many kitchens finish it in pork fat or a chicken stock. The 2026/06 machine shows this button marked SOLD OUT (×).

items.en: Two extra slices of char siu pork
items.note: Soy-braised pork.

items.en: Sapporo Lager 'Red Star', medium bottle
items.note: Barley malt.

items.ja: サッポロ黒ラベル（小瓶）
items.en: Sapporo Black Label, small bottle
items.note: Barley malt.

items.en: Whisky highball
items.note: Whisky is distilled from barley malt.

items.en: Lemon sour
items.note: The base spirit is not named on the machine or the wall card; a sour base in Japan is usually 甲類焼酎, which is distilled and often from molasses or grain. Ask which bottle if it matters.

items.en: Cola — the shop is listed as a 瓶コーク提供店, a bottled-Coke house
items.note: Carbonated soft drink; no gluten grain and no animal ingredient.

tokyo_kaisen_to_robatayaki_iro.price_note: Prices 税込 (tax-included). The 64 food items are the shop's own 公式 Tabelog registration, 更新日 2026/05/21 — the newest card the shop publishes. Two dishes are listed there with the price suppressed (刺身三点盛り, 天ぷら盛り合わせ); both also appear on the shop's own HotPepper page (囲炉裏 新宿本店, strJ003737463, 料理 updated 2025/10/27) with prices, and those figures are used here and flagged in the note. シーザーサラダ is on the 2026/05 card with no price anywhere and is left blank rather than guessed. Courses are from the HotPepper course tab, updated 2026/06/13 — current. The drinks tab has not been touched since 2024/03/04, so drink prices are two years old and only a representative selection is carried. Address confirmed identical on both listings — 東京都新宿区西新宿1-18-13 近江ビル3F — so the HotPepper page is this shop and not a same-name branch (a second Shinjuku 囲炉裏 exists on Tabelog under id 13306691). The shop publishes no allergen information of any kind, which is why nothing below is marked gluten-free except the pure-rice sake.

items.ja: さばの炭火焼き土鍋ご飯
items.en: Charcoal-grilled mackerel cooked into rice in a clay pot
items.note: The house speciality — rice steamed in a 土鍋 with the grilled fish laid on top, brought to the table in the pot. Seasoned clay-pot rice is built on a dashi that in a Japanese kitchen means 白だし or だし醤油, i.e. wheat soy sauce, and the shop confirms no ingredients. Treat as wheat. Plain unseasoned rice is not on the menu.

items.ja: 鮭ハラスといくらの親子土鍋飯
items.romaji: sake harasu to ikura no oyako donabe meshi
items.en: Salmon belly and salmon roe 'parent and child' clay-pot rice
items.note: 親子 (oyako, 'parent and child') because the fish and its own roe share the pot. The Tabelog card renders the name with a stray leading character (こ鮭…); HotPepper's spelling is used. Same seasoned-dashi wheat problem as the other pots, and ikura is cured in a soy-and-sake marinade as standard.

items.ja: 国産牛のすき焼き風土鍋ご飯
items.en: Japanese beef sukiyaki-style clay-pot rice
items.note: すき焼き風 names the seasoning outright: warishita, which is soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Wheat by definition, no ambiguity here.

items.ja: サーモンハラス干し焼き
items.en: Dried and charcoal-grilled salmon belly
items.section: 炉端焼き Robata charcoal grill
items.note: ハラス is the fatty belly strip. 干し (dried) fish is cured in brine, but 醤油干し — a soy-sauce cure — is common and is not distinguishable by looking. Ask whether the cure is 塩 or 醤油, and ask about the grill, which also carries tare-glazed skewers.

items.ja: 伴助ホッケの塩干し焼き
items.en: Bansuke-brand atka mackerel, salt-cured and charcoal-grilled
items.section: 炉端焼き Robata charcoal grill
items.note: 伴助 is a Hokkaido himono producer whose name the shop puts on the menu. 塩干し says the cure is salt, not soy, which makes this one of the less risky things on the grill — but it is cooked over the same charcoal as the tare skewers, so it is an ask rather than a yes.

items.en: Grilled mackerel
items.section: 炉端焼き Robata charcoal grill
items.note: The shop's PR calls its トロサバ (fatty mackerel) robata the signature of the cheaper course. The card does not say whether it is salt-grilled or miso/soy-marinated; ask for 塩焼き and ask about the shared grill.

items.en: Salt-grilled sablefish (black cod)
items.section: 炉端焼き Robata charcoal grill
items.note: 塩焼き means salted and grilled, not the 西京焼き miso marinade that black cod usually gets — worth knowing, because saikyo miso would put barley or soy in the dish. Shared grill is still the open question.

items.ja: うずらのにんにく醤油漬け
items.en: Quail eggs marinated in garlic soy sauce
items.note: 醤油漬け is printed on the menu — soy-sauce marinated, so wheat, and quail eggs are eggs.

items.en: Salted green soy beans in the pod
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: Boiled in salted water and nothing else in the standard preparation, which makes it the plainest thing on this menu and the obvious vegan order. It is only an ask on gluten because the shop publishes no ingredients at all and some izakaya toss edamame in a garlic-soy or chilli dressing — confirm it is 塩茹で only.

items.en: Shark cartilage dressed with pickled-plum paste
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: 'Plum crystal' — chopped shark cartilage, crunchy and translucent, in a sour umeboshi dressing. It is a dressed dish and the dressing is normally built with soy sauce and mirin; with no ingredient list published, treat as wheat.

items.en: Squid fermented in its own salted innards
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: Intense, salty and boozy — a classic sake chaser. Traditional shiokara is squid, its liver and salt, which would be wheat-free, but commercial tubs routinely add 醤油, 味醂 or 酒精 and this kitchen does not say which it uses.

items.en: Rolled omelette soaked with dashi
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: Egg, so never vegan; and the dashi it is rolled with is the wheat problem, because a Japanese kitchen builds it from 白だし or だし醤油 rather than kombu and water. Bonito is in there too.

items.en: Korean-style chilli-marinated cod stomach
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: A Korean-Japanese izakaya staple: salted cod tripe in a gochujang-based marinade. Gochujang is normally wheat-thickened and the marinade usually carries soy sauce and fish sauce as well.

items.en: Raw octopus in wasabi stem dressing
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: Diced raw octopus with chopped wasabi stalk in a sticky seasoning. The seasoning is the risk — commercial tako-wasa bases are soy-sauce and mirin based — and octopus is not vegan.

items.en: Three-item assortment of the salty fermented nibbles
items.section: 酒肴逸品 Small plates for drinking
items.note: 珍味 means the fermented/cured delicacies — in practice a plate combining three of the shiokara, chanja, ume-suisho and tako-wasa above. It inherits every soy-sauce risk they carry, and cannot be unpicked once plated.

items.en: Seafood salad
items.note: Leaves under sashimi-grade fish. The leaves and the fish are both wheat-free; the wheat, if it is there, is in the poured dressing — Japanese 和風ドレッシング is soy-sauce based. Dressings are the one thing a kitchen can swap on request, so ask for oil and salt and this becomes orderable.

items.en: Whitebait salad
items.note: しらす are tiny boiled sardine fry, scattered whole over the leaves. Same answer as the seafood salad: ask what the dressing is and whether it can be left off.

items.en: Japanese potato salad
items.note: Bound with Kewpie mayonnaise, which is egg — so not vegan. Japanese mayonnaise itself is wheat-free, but izakaya potato salad commonly has ham or bacon folded through and sometimes a splash of soy; ask.

items.en: Caesar salad
items.note: Price not published — it is the one line on the 2026/05 card with the figure suppressed, and it is absent from the older HotPepper list, so no honest number exists. Caesar means croutons (wheat), parmesan and an egg-and-anchovy dressing; wheat is in the bowl, not merely on the side.

items.en: Chicken thigh skewer
items.note: The plain thigh skewer. Every skewer here is the same question: 塩 (salt) or タレ (glaze). Tare is a soy-sauce reduction, so it is wheat; ask for 塩 and ask whether the salt skewers are cooked over the same bars and brushed with the same brush.

items.en: Chicken skin skewer
items.note: Crisped chicken skin. Salt or tare — tare is wheat soy sauce.

items.en: Breastbone cartilage skewer
items.note: The soft keel cartilage from the chicken's breastbone — eaten for the crunch. Salt or tare; tare is wheat.

items.en: Tongue skewer
items.note: Tongue, usually beef or pork at an izakaya rather than chicken. Salt or tare; tare is wheat.

items.en: Chicken and spring onion skewer
items.note: Alternating thigh and Japanese leek — the default yakitori order. Salt or tare; tare is wheat.

items.en: Chicken tail skewer
items.note: The fatty parson's nose, one skewer per bird. Salt or tare; tare is wheat.

items.en: Cheek and temple meat skewer
items.note: かしら is head meat, normally pork — a yakiton rather than a yakitori. Salt or tare; tare is wheat.

items.en: 'Angel prawn' skewer
items.note: 天使の海老 is a branded blue shrimp farmed in New Caledonia, sold whole and shell-on. Grilled rather than battered, so the wheat question is only the seasoning and the shared grill — but shellfish is its own major allergen.

items.en: Five assorted skewers
items.note: The chef picks the five. That means you cannot control which arrive tare-glazed, so a wheat-avoiding diner is better ordering singles 塩 than taking the assortment.

items.en: Eight assorted skewers
items.note: The larger chef's assortment; same caveat about not choosing the glaze.

items.en: Tuna sashimi
items.note: Raw fish is naturally wheat-free; the wheat arrives with the soy sauce it is dipped in. Carrying a small bottle of tamari makes the whole sashimi section orderable.

items.en: Yellowtail sashimi
items.note: Raw fish; soy sauce is the gluten risk, not the fish.

items.en: Salmon sashimi
items.note: Raw fish; soy sauce is the gluten risk.

items.en: Vinegar-cured mackerel
items.note: Cured in salt then rice vinegar, both wheat-free — but many kitchens finish the cure with a splash of soy or mirin, and it is eaten with soy at the table.

items.en: Raw horse sashimi
items.note: A Kumamoto speciality that has become a standard izakaya order. Served with grated garlic and ginger and a soy dip — the dip is the wheat.

items.en: Three-kind sashimi platter
items.note: Price is suppressed on the shop's 2026/05 Tabelog card; ¥1,780 is the figure on the shop's own HotPepper list, last updated 2025/10/27, so treat it as indicative rather than today's number. Raw fish, soy sauce is the risk.

items.en: Five-kind sashimi platter
items.note: The shop's PR builds the whole restaurant around its 刺身の桶盛り — sashimi cut deliberately thick, served in a wooden tub. Raw fish; the soy is the wheat.

items.en: Deep-fried chicken cartilage
items.note: 唐揚げ is dusted in wheat flour or a flour-and-potato-starch mix and soaked first in a soy-and-sake marinade. Both halves are wheat, and the fryer is shared with everything else in this section and the tempura.

items.en: Deep-fried octopus
items.note: Same karaage coating and marinade as the chicken cartilage — wheat flour and soy — plus a shared fryer.

items.en: Chips / french fries
items.note: Potato and oil contain no wheat, but they go into the same fryer as the karaage, the tempura and the フライ — so the oil carries wheat and this is not a coeliac order. For a vegan the fryer is a judgement call rather than a bar; the other question is whether they come dusted with a seasoned salt.

items.ja: さつまいもスティック
items.en: Sweet potato fries
items.note: Sweet potato batons. Plant-based in themselves, but shared fryer with wheat-battered items, and Japanese sweet-potato sticks are often finished with butter or honey — ask.

items.en: Fried octopus with grated daikon and ponzu
items.note: Two separate wheat sources: the karaage flour, and ponzu, which is soy sauce cut with citrus. Here the sauce is poured over rather than served on the side.

items.en: Fried burdock root sticks
items.note: Burdock cut into matchsticks and fried crisp; usually dusted in flour or starch before frying, and always the shared fryer.

items.en: Fried fish cake with vegetables
items.note: The name has 野菜 in it but satsuma-age is a fish-paste cake — surimi — so it is not vegetarian at all. Commercial surimi is bound with wheat starch and seasoned with soy, then deep-fried.

items.en: Crumbed sardine rolled with plum paste and perilla
items.note: フライ means panko-crumbed — bread, i.e. wheat, before you even reach the flour-and-egg wash.

items.en: Onion rings
items.note: Battered or crumbed onion — wheat in the coating, and the batter commonly carries egg and milk as well.

items.en: Deep-fried squid
items.note: Karaage flour coating and shared fryer.

items.en: Deep-fried wakame seaweed
items.note: An unusual order — seaweed fried until it shatters. Vegan in substance if the batter has no egg and the oil is not shared with fish, neither of which is stated; the flour coating rules it out for gluten regardless.

items.ja: シャキシャキ！蓮根七味
items.en: Crunchy lotus root with seven-spice
items.note: シャキシャキ is the onomatopoeia for the crunch. Lotus root fried and dusted with shichimi — the spice blend itself is wheat-free, but the coating and the shared fryer are not. Shichimi does often contain sesame and citrus peel.

items.en: Sweet potato tempura
items.note: Tempura batter is wheat flour, and the classic batter is bound with egg. The dipping tsuyu is dashi plus soy sauce — wheat and bonito both. Nothing in this section can be made gluten-free.

items.en: Squid tempura
items.note: Wheat batter, shared fryer, soy-based tsuyu.

items.en: Hen-of-the-woods mushroom tempura
items.note: Maitake takes to tempura better than almost any vegetable. Still wheat batter, likely egg in it, and a fryer shared with prawn and squid.

items.en: Prawn tempura
items.note: Wheat batter, shared fryer, soy-based tsuyu.

items.en: Scallop tempura
items.note: Wheat batter, shared fryer, soy-based tsuyu.

items.en: Tube fish cake fried in seaweed batter
items.note: 磯部 means aonori seaweed stirred into the batter. Doubly wheat: chikuwa is a surimi fish stick normally bound with wheat starch, and the batter is flour. Not vegetarian either.

items.en: Assorted tempura platter
items.note: Price suppressed on the shop's 2026/05 Tabelog card; ¥1,680 comes from the shop's own HotPepper list of 2025/10/27, so it is indicative rather than confirmed for today. Wheat batter throughout.

items.ja: 鮭といくらの親子寿司
items.romaji: sake to ikura no oyako sushi
items.en: Salmon and salmon-roe 'parent and child' sushi
items.note: Sushi rice is rice, vinegar, sugar and salt — no wheat — but the roe is cured in a soy-and-sake marinade and sushi is normally brushed with nikiri, a thinned soy. Ask.

items.ja: かにレタスチャーハン
items.en: Crab and lettuce fried rice
items.note: Fried rice is finished with soy sauce as a matter of course, contains egg, and the 'crab' at this price point is often kanikama surimi sticks, which are wheat-bound.

items.en: Salt-seasoned seafood fried noodles
items.note: 塩 in the name means it skips the brown yakisoba sauce — but yakisoba noodles are wheat noodles despite the word そば, so this is wheat at the core, not in the seasoning.

items.ja: ズワイガニとウニの贅沢握り
items.romaji: zuwaigani to uni no zeitaku nigiri
items.en: Extravagant snow crab and sea urchin nigiri
items.note: The most expensive single plate outside the clay pots, and the headline of the ¥6,000 course. Crab and uni themselves are wheat-free; nigiri is normally brushed with nikiri soy, and uni is often stabilised with alum rather than anything wheaty. Ask about the brush.

items.en: Vanilla ice cream
items.note: Dairy and usually egg, so not vegan. Ice cream is normally wheat-free, but bought-in tubs can carry wheat-derived stabilisers and it may arrive with a wafer — ask.

items.en: House-made baked custard pudding
items.note: 自家製 — made in house. Egg, milk and caramelised sugar; a baked custard has no flour in it by construction, but it is baked in a kitchen with no allergen statement.

items.en: Matcha sponge roll
items.note: A rolled sponge is wheat flour and egg, with dairy cream inside. No version of this is safe.

items.en: Matcha ice cream
items.note: Dairy. Same caveat as the vanilla about bought-in tubs and wafers.

items.en: Strawberry sponge roll
items.note: Wheat sponge, egg, dairy cream.

items.ja: 『特別蘭コース』全9品 3時間生ビール付飲み放題
items.en: 'Special Orchid' course — 9 dishes with 3 hours of all-you-can-drink including draught beer
items.note: The entry course. The shop names the angel-prawn skewer and a scallop-butter robata as its centrepieces — butter, so not vegan, and the courses all pass through the tempura and karaage sections. Booked online; 2 people minimum. Course tab updated 2026/06/13.

items.ja: 『特別竹コース』全10品 3時間生ビール付飲み放題
items.en: 'Special Bamboo' course — 10 dishes with 3 hours of all-you-can-drink including draught beer
items.note: Adds the salmon-and-ikura clay-pot rice, robata grills and grilled beef skirt. The shop describes it as including 京出汁おでん — Kyoto-style dashi oden, which is simmered in a soy-seasoned broth, so the wheat is in the liquid.

items.ja: 【松コース】全11品 3時間生ビール付飲み放題
items.en: 'Pine' course — 11 dishes with 3 hours of all-you-can-drink including draught beer
items.note: Charcoal-grilled Oyama chicken, grilled salmon with ikura and an oden assortment. Oden broth and the all-you-can-drink beer both put wheat on the table.

items.ja: ズワイガニと雲丹の贅沢握り含む全12品 3時間生ビール付飲み放題
items.en: Top course, 12 dishes including the snow crab and uni nigiri, with 3 hours of all-you-can-drink
items.note: The flagship: sashimi platter, tempura, the crab-and-uni nigiri and a spicy chicken. Bookable for 2 to 110 people. Tempura and oden mean wheat is unavoidable in the sequence.

items.en: Drinks-only all-you-can-drink plan (limited period)
items.note: No food attached — the plan exists so you can order à la carte and still drink flat-rate. Advertised as ¥2,700 reduced to ¥1,980 before tax; ¥2,178 is the tax-included figure the booking page charges. Includes beer, which is barley malt, so the plan as sold is not gluten-free even though individual drinks within it might be.

items.ja: ザ・プレミアムモルツ(中ジョッキ)
items.en: Suntory Premium Malt's draught, medium mug
items.note: Barley malt beer — gluten, no exceptions. Fining agents mean beer is not automatically vegan either. Drink prices on the shop's HotPepper page have not been revised since 2024/03/04.

items.ja: ≪ノンアルコール≫オールフリー
items.en: Suntory All-Free alcohol-free beer
items.note: Alcohol-free is not gluten-free: All-Free is brewed from barley malt like any other beer. This is the trap that catches people who assume the 0.00% option is the safe one.

items.ja: 獺祭50 純米大吟醸(一合)
items.en: Dassai 50 junmai daiginjo sake, 180ml carafe
items.note: 純米 means rice, rice-koji and water and nothing else — no brewer's alcohol, no wheat, no animal product. Poured from a sealed bottle, so nothing in this kitchen can contaminate it. The single safest thing on the whole list for a coeliac. 一合 is 180ml.

items.ja: 獺祭 磨き三割九分 純米大吟醸(一合)
items.romaji: Dassai migaki sanwari kyubu junmai daiginjo (ichi-go)
items.en: Dassai 39 junmai daiginjo sake, 180ml carafe
items.note: 三割九分 = the rice polished down to 39% of its original grain. Junmai, so rice and koji only — wheat-free and plant-based.

items.ja: 梵　ときしらず 濃醇辛口純米大吟醸(一合)
items.en: Born 'Tokishirazu' rich dry junmai daiginjo, 180ml carafe
items.note: A Fukui sake aged cold before release — ときしらず means 'out of season'. Junmai: rice, koji, water.

items.en: Urakasumi junmai sake, 180ml carafe
items.note: Miyagi's benchmark brewery, a standard izakaya pour. Junmai — rice and koji only.

items.ja: 大隅(麦)/一粒の麦(麦)/中々(麦)
items.romaji: mugi shochu (Osumi / Hitotsubu no Mugi / Nakanaka)
items.en: Barley shochu, by the glass — on the rocks, with water or with hot water
items.note: 麦 is barley. Distillation removes gluten protein in principle, but barley shochu is the drink most likely to be handled and served alongside barley product, and this app does not flag any 麦 drink as safe. Order 芋 or 米 instead if you must have shochu.

items.ja: 大隅(芋)/黒丸(芋)/黒霧島(芋)/富乃宝山(芋)/海(芋)
items.romaji: imo shochu (Osumi / Kuromaru / Kuro-Kirishima / Tomi no Hozan / Umi)
items.en: Sweet-potato shochu, by the glass
items.note: Distilled from sweet potato, but the koji starter for imo shochu is usually rice and occasionally barley — ask which. Plant-based either way.

items.en: Rice shochu, by the glass
items.note: Rice base with rice koji — no grain other than rice is involved in either of these Kumamoto labels. Marked ask only because the shop publishes nothing about how it is poured.

items.ja: こだわり酒場のレモンサワー
items.en: Lemon sour made with Suntory's izakaya-style shochu base
items.note: The cheapest drink on the list. Shochu, lemon and soda; the base spirit is a blended shochu whose grain is unstated on the shop's card. No animal ingredient.

items.ja: ウーロンハイ/緑茶ハイ
items.en: Oolong tea or green tea mixed with shochu
items.note: Worth knowing as the non-beer default: oolong and green tea are both leaf tea, not barley, so unlike 麦茶 they bring no gluten of their own. The open question is only which shochu is under them.

tokyo_naan_house_suidobashi.price_note: The shop registers no menu on Tabelog (料理 0 / ドリンク 0) and has no website; everything below is transcribed from photographs of the shop's own printed cards and its own street A-board, read at full resolution. Three separate dates are in play and each item says which it came from. (1) The laminated lunch card photographed 2026/04 — the current one, crisp and unambiguous, sets A–H at ¥900–950. (2) The same shop's earlier lunch card photographed 2025/08 ran ¥820–900 with a different A–H lettering, so both the lettering and the prices were re-issued between those dates — do not trust an older transcription of the letters. (3) The street A-board, photographed 2024/04 (legible) and again 2026/04 (same board, same layout, but the SET/BENTO price panels have been re-stickered and are unreadable in the newer shot). À-la-carte figures below are therefore the 2024/04 readings, two years old, and the set-box prices from that board are deliberately omitted because the shop has since changed them. Drinks come from the shop's DRINK MENU card photographed 2023/04 and are three years old — treat as indicative only. One unresolved oddity: a 2025/10 photo in the same gallery shows a card headed 「アジアン料理 ナンハウス」 with a Thai flag and a ¥1,000–1,200 Thai lunch line-up, which does not match the shop's own Indo-Nepalese signage; it is not used here. Address confirmed 東京都千代田区神田三崎町2-15-9 小暮ビル1F on Tabelog, on Retty and on the building sign visible beside the A-board. Naan is baked on the premises, so wheat flour is airborne in this kitchen — that is the background risk behind every 'ask' below.

items.ja: Aセット チキンカレー
items.en: Chicken curry set: curry, naan or rice, salad and a soft drink
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Every A–H set is one curry with naan OR rice, a salad and a set drink, and the card promises one free refill of the naan or the rice (ナン又はライス一回おかわり出来ます). Taking rice instead of naan removes the obvious wheat, but the curry base itself is the unanswered question — ask whether the sauce is thickened with 小麦粉 or with onion and tomato only. Chicken, so not vegan.

items.ja: Bセット 野菜カレー
items.en: Vegetable curry set
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: The one set with no meat in the curry itself, so it is the starting point for a vegan — but Indian and Nepalese vegetable curries are routinely finished with ghee, butter or cream, and the set includes naan (milk and yogurt are normal in naan dough) and a salad dressing. Ask for it made with oil, take rice instead of naan, and check the dressing.

items.ja: Cセット 日替わりカレー
items.en: Curry-of-the-day set
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: 日替わり means it changes daily and is not written down anywhere, so you have to ask what today's is before you can ask anything else about it.

items.ja: Dセット ラムカレー
items.en: Lamb curry set
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Lamb. The 2025/08 card had a マトンカレー (mutton) in this slot instead; the 2026/04 card says ラム.

items.ja: Eセット キーマカレー
items.en: Minced-meat keema curry set
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Keema is minced meat, normally chicken or mutton, cooked dry with peas. Minced-meat curries are the ones most often bulked out with flour — worth asking specifically.

items.ja: Fセット ほうれん草チキンカレー
items.en: Spinach and chicken (saag) curry set
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Saag chicken — the deep green curry in the photograph. Spinach curries are usually finished with cream or butter as well as the chicken.

items.ja: Gセット シーフードカレー
items.en: Seafood curry set
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Called ミックスシーフードカレー on the older card. Prawn and mixed seafood, so shellfish as well as the curry-base question.

items.ja: Hセット バターチキンカレー
items.en: Butter chicken curry set
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Butter, cream and yogurt by definition — the single least vegan curry on the list, and the mildest, which is why it is the one Japanese menus put in the ladies' set.

items.en: Two-curry set: naan, rice, salad, the curry of the day plus one curry from A–H, chicken tikka 1pc and a soft drink
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: The card spells out the contents: ナン、ライス、サラダ、日替わりカレー、カレー1種(A〜H)、チキンティッカ1p、ソフトドリンク. Naan is included rather than offered as an alternative, so wheat is on the plate, and the chicken tikka makes it non-vegan.

items.en: Ladies' set: salad, curry of the day, butter chicken curry, naan, rice and a soft drink
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Contents printed on the card: サラダ、日替わりカレー、バターチキンカレー、ナン、ライス、ソフトドリンク. Both naan and butter chicken are fixed, so this one cannot be adjusted around.

items.en: Cheese naan set: one curry from A–H, cheese naan, salad and a soft drink
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Cheese naan is wheat dough stuffed with melted cheese — wheat and dairy, and the naan is the point of the set so there is no swap.

items.en: Thai holy-basil minced meat over rice, with salad and a soft drink
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: The Thai outlier on an Indo-Nepalese card. Gapao is built on fish sauce, oyster sauce and soy sauce — oyster sauce is thickened with wheat as standard and soy sauce is wheat — and it is served with a fried egg on top. Rice-based, but not a safe rice dish.

items.ja: セットのナン変更（ごまナン／アンコナン／ガーリクナン）
items.en: Upgrade the set's plain naan to sesame, sweet-bean or garlic naan
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Printed across the top of the card. アンコナン is naan stuffed with sweetened red bean paste — a dessert naan. All three are wheat; the anko one is the only naan on the menu with a plausibly dairy-free filling, but the dough itself usually is not.

items.ja: 辛さ（甘口・普通・中辛・辛口・激辛）
items.en: Spice level: mild, medium, hot, very hot, extra hot
items.section: ランチセット Lunch sets (2026/04 card)
items.note: Not a dish — the five-step heat scale printed on the card, which you are asked to choose when ordering any curry. The A-board prints the same scale numbered 0 甘口 (Mild) / 1 普通 (Medium) / 2 中辛 (Hot) / 3 辛口 (Very Hot), so quoting a number works if the words do not. Vegan status was left blank by an earlier pass and is not established by any source read; recorded as ask. Gluten status was left blank by an earlier pass and is not established by any source read; recorded as ask.

items.en: Tandoor-grilled boneless chicken, one piece (lunch add-on)
items.section: サイドメニュー Lunch side menu (2026/04 card)
items.note: Lunch add-on price for a single piece; the à-la-carte board sells a larger portion for ¥380. Tikka is chicken marinated in yogurt and spice then cooked in the tandoor — no wheat in the classical recipe, but bought-in tandoori pastes are the usual place wheat hides, and the tandoor is the same oven the naan is slapped onto.

items.en: Tandoor-roasted chicken on the bone, one piece (lunch add-on)
items.section: サイドメニュー Lunch side menu (2026/04 card)
items.note: Same marinade question as the tikka. The A-board prices this at ¥200, so the two cards disagree by ¥50 — the lunch card is the newer of the two.

items.en: Nepalese steamed dumplings, six pieces
items.section: サイドメニュー Lunch side menu (2026/04 card)
items.note: The Nepalese dish on the menu and the one worth ordering for its own sake. The wrapper is wheat flour and water — momo is never gluten-free. The filling is not stated on either card; Nepalese shops in Japan default to minced chicken, so ask before assuming a vegetable version exists. The board price is ¥580 for the same six pieces.

items.en: Fried pastry triangles with spiced potato, two pieces
items.section: サイドメニュー Lunch side menu (2026/04 card)
items.note: The pastry is wheat, fried — wheat twice over. The potato-and-pea filling is usually plant-based but the pastry is often shortened with ghee. Board price ¥450 for two.

items.ja: セットドリンク（ラッシー／マンゴーラッシー／ウーロン茶／マンゴージュース／チャイ／コーヒー）
items.en: Set drink, included: lassi, mango lassi, oolong tea, mango juice, chai (hot or iced) or coffee (hot or iced)
items.section: サイドメニュー Lunch side menu (2026/04 card)
items.note: Six choices, included in every lunch set. Oolong tea and mango juice are the two with no dairy in them — the lassis and the chai are both milk-based, which matters for a vegan far more than for a coeliac. Oolong is leaf tea, not 麦茶, so it carries no barley.

items.en: Fresh rice-paper spring rolls, two pieces
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Vietnamese-style cold rolls. Rice paper is rice and tapioca, so the wrapper itself is wheat-free — unusually for this menu. The risk moves entirely to the dipping sauce (hoisin is wheat-thickened, sweet chilli usually is not) and to whether there is prawn or pork inside, which the board does not say.

items.en: Tandoor-grilled boneless chicken
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: The full à-la-carte portion, larger than the ¥200 single lunch piece. Yogurt-and-spice marinade cooked in the naan oven.

items.en: Tandoor-grilled marinated fish, two pieces
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Fish in the same red tandoori marinade. Some kitchens dust fish tikka with besan (gram flour), which is gluten-free, and some use plain flour — ask which.

items.en: Nepalese steamed dumplings, six pieces
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Wheat wrapper. The board photograph shows them plain-steamed with a bowl of orange achar dipping sauce.

items.en: Fried spiced-potato pastries, two pieces
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Wheat pastry, deep-fried; the board shows them served with two dips.

items.en: Salted green soy beans in the pod
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: The cheapest thing on the board and, in a kitchen where naan flour is in the air, the item with the fewest ingredients — boiled soybeans and salt. Vegan without qualification. Gluten is an ask only because nothing here is prepared in a segregated space.

items.en: Spiced minced-meat skewers, two pieces
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Minced meat pressed onto a skewer and cooked in the tandoor. Minced-meat kebabs are commonly bound with breadcrumbs or besan — which one decides the answer, and the board does not say.

items.en: Thai hot and sour prawn soup
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Prawn and fish sauce, so not vegan. Fish sauce is usually just anchovy and salt, but Thai chilli pastes and stock powders often carry wheat — ask.

items.en: Indonesian fried rice with a fried egg
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Nasi goreng is seasoned with kecap manis, the thick Indonesian sweet soy sauce, and Japanese kitchens reach for ordinary soy sauce alongside it — wheat either way. The board photograph shows it topped with a fried egg and served with prawn crackers.

items.en: Tandoor-roasted chicken on the bone
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: The cheapest protein on the board. The lunch card sells the same single piece for ¥250, so this 2024 figure may have moved.

items.en: Marinated lamb chops, two pieces
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Bone-in lamb from the tandoor, the most substantial single plate on the board short of a curry.

items.en: Green salad
items.section: 一品料理 À la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Leaves, cucumber and red cabbage in the board photograph, with dressing already poured. The dressing is the whole question — Japanese restaurant dressings are commonly soy-sauce or mayonnaise based. Ask for it undressed and it becomes the safest plate in the room.

items.en: Chicken masala curry, with naan or rice included
items.section: カレー Curries à la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: The board prints 「カレーの値段にはナン又はライス付き」— the curry price already includes naan or rice, so ask for rice and you are not paying extra to avoid the wheat. The curry base itself still needs asking about.

items.en: Spinach and chicken curry, with naan or rice included
items.section: カレー Curries à la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Saag chicken. Cream or butter is normal in the finish as well as the chicken.

items.en: Butter chicken curry, with naan or rice included
items.section: カレー Curries à la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Butter, cream, yogurt and chicken.

items.en: Mutton masala curry, with naan or rice included
items.section: カレー Curries à la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Goat or mature sheep, cooked long. Read at high magnification off the board photograph; the figure is legible as 980円.

items.en: Chickpea curry, with naan or rice included
items.section: カレー Curries à la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Chickpeas in a tomato and onion masala — the classic North Indian dish that is plant-based in its home version, and the best vegan candidate on the board alongside the aubergine. Whether this kitchen finishes it with ghee or butter is the thing to ask, along with taking rice rather than the included naan.

items.en: Aubergine masala curry, with naan or rice included
items.section: カレー Curries à la carte (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Baigan (aubergine) masala. The price tag on the board photograph sits at the edge of the frame and could not be read at any magnification, so it is left empty rather than guessed — the neighbouring curries run ¥780–980. Same vegan question as the chana: ghee or oil.

items.en: Garlic naan
items.note: Naan is refined wheat flour baked on the wall of the tandoor. There is no version of this dish that a coeliac can eat, and this is the oven that puts flour into the air of the whole kitchen. Naan dough usually contains milk or yogurt, which is why the vegan answer is ask rather than yes.

items.en: Small cheese-stuffed naan
items.note: Wheat dough with melted cheese sealed inside. Wheat and dairy.

items.ja: Aベントー（テイクアウト）
items.en: Takeaway A: one curry with naan or turmeric rice
items.section: テイクアウト Takeaway (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: The takeaway board lets you pick from six curries — ①チキン ②キーマ ③マトン ④エビ ⑤ほうれん草&チキン ⑥野菜 — and choose naan or ターメリックライス. Choosing the vegetable curry with turmeric rice is the closest thing to a wheat-free order here, though turmeric rice is usually started in butter or ghee.

items.ja: Bベントー（テイクアウト）
items.en: Takeaway B: one curry with naan and turmeric rice, salad and chicken tikka 1pc
items.section: テイクアウト Takeaway (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Naan is included rather than alternative, and a piece of chicken tikka comes with it.

items.ja: Cテイクアウト タイのガパオライス
items.en: Takeaway C: Thai holy-basil rice
items.section: テイクアウト Takeaway (street board, 2024/04)
items.note: Same dish as the lunch set — soy, oyster and fish sauce, topped with a fried egg.

items.ja: キリン一番搾り 生ビール
items.en: Kirin Ichiban Shibori draught beer
items.note: Barley malt — gluten. The card also lists a pitcher at ¥1,300 and a bottle at ¥520. Drink prices are from a 2023/04 photograph of the shop's own drink card and are three years old.

items.ja: ワールドビール（インド／ネパール／コロナ／シンハー／バーバーバー／サイゴン）
items.en: Imported bottled beers: Indian, Nepali, Corona, Singha, Bia Ba Ba Ba, Saigon — all one price
items.note: Six countries at a flat ¥600. All barley beers, including the Nepali one (Mt. Everest / Gorkha). A separate window poster offers a free piece of tandoori chicken and a papad with any Nepali beer — 「ネパールのビールを一本注文頂きましたらタンドリーチキン1p。とパパド1枚無料致します」— worth knowing, though the papad is chickpea flour and the offer was posted in 2024.

items.en: Hakusui barley shochu, single
items.note: 麦 is barley. Double ¥680, bottle ¥3,080 on the same card. Not flagged safe here — order the sweet-potato one instead.

items.ja: 焼酎 まろやか芋／宝山（芋）
items.en: Sweet-potato shochu, single
items.note: Distilled from sweet potato; the koji starter is usually rice but occasionally barley, which is the only reason this is not a yes. Double ¥680; 宝山 bottle ¥3,080. Plant-based.

items.ja: サワー各種（レモン／ライム／グレープフルーツ／ウーロンハイ／オレンジ／梅干し）
items.en: Shochu sours — lemon, lime, grapefruit, oolong, orange or pickled plum, all one price
items.note: The cheapest alcohol on the card. Shochu, fruit or tea, and soda; the open question is which shochu is under them. The oolong one carries no barley of its own, unlike a 麦茶ハイ would.

items.ja: ハウスワイン フランジア（赤／白）
items.en: House wine, red or white, by the glass
items.note: Wine is fermented grape juice — no grain is involved at any stage, so it carries no gluten. Vegan is a genuine ask because wine is often fined with egg white, casein or isinglass. Decanter ¥1,200, bottle ¥1,600; an Indian wine is also listed at ¥2,500 the bottle.

items.ja: インドウイスキーハイボール
items.en: Indian whisky highball
items.note: Whisky is a grain spirit and this app does not flag any whisky or highball as gluten-free. A White Horse highball is also listed at ¥350, and singles across the whisky and rum list are a flat ¥450 (doubles ¥800), including Khukuri Rum, the Nepali army rum.

items.en: Yogurt drink
items.note: Yogurt, water and sugar, blended to order — three ingredients, none of them grain, and nothing that touches the tandoor. Dairy, so squarely not vegan. Mango lassi ¥400.

items.en: Oolong tea
items.note: Oolong is the leaf of the tea plant, not a roasted grain — worth stating because its shelf-neighbour 麦茶 (barley tea) is the Japanese soft drink that will glutenate you. Nothing but leaf and water here. A ¥400 decanter is listed under トッピング for topping up shochu.

items.en: Hot spiced milk tea
items.note: Tea simmered in milk with cardamom, cinnamon and ginger. Milk, so not vegan; the spice blend is the only place wheat could hide and it very rarely does. Iced version ¥300.

items.ja: マンゴージュース／オレンジ／グレープフルーツ／コーラ
items.en: Mango, orange or grapefruit juice, or cola
items.note: The dairy-free soft drinks, and the ones to pick as your included lunch set drink if you are avoiding milk. Poured from cartons and bottles.

items.en: Cocktails — vodka, cassis, Campari, Dita, gin, Malibu, mojito, Kahlua or wine base, all one price
items.note: A long grid of bases each crossed with soda, orange, grapefruit, oolong, lassi or tonic, at a flat ¥400. Vodka and gin are grain spirits, so a coeliac who avoids grain distillates should ask which base is used; nothing in the list is animal-derived.

tokyo_kita_no_shoyu_chi_ho_sui.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Every figure below is read off the shop's OWN touch-panel ticket machine (券売機) and its OWN printed メニュー表, photographed at full resolution and cross-checked across three dates: the 外メニュー sheet taped to the shutter in 2026/05, the ticket-machine screens in 2026/07, and the メニュー表 + お並びのご案内 posters on the wall in 2026/08. The three ramen prices are identical in all three, so these are current, not a stale card. Dated 2026/08 diners independently quote 特製ラーメン 1,500円, 誠意のチャーシュー丼 450円, 北ノ醤油ラーメン 1,100円 and 西の汁なし 1,100円 — an exact match. THE SHOP HAS NO WEBSITE: Tabelog lists no ホームページ and there is no 公式 registration, only an X and an Instagram account; the ticket-machine photograph is therefore the authoritative document here. WHAT THIS SHOP IS: the first bricks-and-mortar shop of the ramen YouTuber SUSURU (すするTV), produced with 俺の生きる道, opened 2026-03-25 at 東京都千代田区神田三崎町2-16-10, 328m from Suidobashi Station. 12 seats (8 counter + two 2-tops), 11:00-22:00 straight through, no closing day, no reservations, CASH ONLY — the machine's own instruction strip reads 商品選択→決定→カートへ進む→お会計→画面中央現金→現金挿入→OK. Queue management is formalised on a printed poster (列A on the left of the frontage, buy your ticket after being called, then join 列B), which tells you to expect 30-50 people. A second branch, 北ノ醤油チーホー つくば店, opened 2026-06-15 at 茨城県つくば市天久保3丁目8-1 — prices there are not evidenced here, so do not carry these across. THERE IS NO ALLERGEN CHART, no allergen notice in the window and no gluten-free anything. The bowl is a 醤油 built like a Sapporo miso: diners describe a kansui-heavy yellow crinkled noodle coloured with 梔子 (gardenia), a ginger-forward 豚骨・鶏ガラ broth with 背脂, and stir-fried moyashi and minced pork on top. The single most useful thing on the counter for a wheat-avoiding reader is the 卓上調味料 card, because it names the seasonings — and the first one on it is かえし, i.e. neat soy-sauce tare, sitting in a bottle within arm's reach of every bowl.

items.en: Kita-no-Shoyu Ramen — the house bowl and the shop's namesake, the top-left button on the ticket machine. Comes with バラチャーシュー2枚, two slices of rolled pork-belly chashu. Diners describe it as a Sapporo-miso bowl rebuilt in soy: a yellow crinkled noodle, a ginger-forward pork-bone and chicken-frame broth carrying back fat, stir-fried bean sprouts and minced pork, and a heap of shredded white onion
items.section: ラーメン Ramen (券売機 ticket machine)
items.note: Wheat three times over. The noodle is a kansui wheat noodle — reviewers specifically call it 鹹水臭い縮れ麺, which is a wheat-and-alkaline-salt noodle by definition. The shop's whole identity is 醤油, and Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat by default; no tamari or gluten-free soy is named anywhere. And the table card names かえし — concentrated soy tare — as the seasoning you are invited to add. Pork-bone and chicken broth plus pork chashu and minced pork, so not vegan either. There is no gluten-free noodle and no allergen chart in this shop.

items.en: Special Ramen — the loaded version of the house bowl: 半熟卵＋バラチャーシュー4枚, a soft-centred seasoned egg plus four slices of belly chashu instead of two. The most-ordered bowl in 2026/08 write-ups
items.section: ラーメン Ramen (券売機 ticket machine)
items.note: Same wheat noodle and same soy tare as the standard bowl, and the two extras it adds are themselves the soy-cured items: a 半熟煮卵 is marinated in soy sauce and chashu is braised in a soy liquor. The deluxe bowl is the most wheat-exposed on the machine, not the least. Not vegan (egg, pork).

items.ja: チャーシューラーメン
items.en: Chashu Ramen — the bowl buried in pork: バラチャーシュー5枚＋厚切りチャーシュー1枚, five belly slices plus one thick-cut slab. The most expensive button on the machine
items.section: ラーメン Ramen (券売機 ticket machine)
items.note: Wheat noodle in a soy tare, and then six pieces of soy-braised pork on top. Nothing here is wheat-free or vegan.

items.en: "Western" soupless noodles — the shop's brothless bowl, with スープ・追い飯無料 printed under it: a cup of the ramen soup AND a follow-on scoop of rice to finish the sauce with are both included free. Diners in 2026/08 praise it for 味変, the run of seasoning changes you make as you eat. A 特製 (loaded) version of it also appears in 2026/08 reviews, but no price for that is published anywhere I could read
items.section: ラーメン Ramen (券売機 ticket machine)
items.note: Wheat noodle again, and a soupless bowl concentrates rather than dilutes the tare — the sauce clinging to these noodles is the soy seasoning at full strength. The free 追い飯 rice is then stirred into that same sauce, so it is not a wheat-free way to eat here. Not vegan. TIMING NOTE, because it matters: on the 2026/07 ticket-machine screen this button was still marked "Coming Soon" and it is absent from the printed 2026/08 メニュー表, yet several 2026/08 diners record ordering and eating it at ¥1,100. Treat it as live but confirm at the machine.

items.en: "Sincerity" Chashu Bowl — a rice bowl of the shop's chashu, the first line on the ticket machine's トッピング/option screen and the priciest add-on. Starred (★) on the machine, which marks the rice-based extras as a group. Repeatedly the second thing 2026/08 diners order
items.section: 追加トッピング Add-on options (10個まで選択)
items.note: The rice underneath is wheat-free but the pork on top is not: chashu is braised in a soy-sauce liquor and these bowls are normally finished with a spoonful of that same braising liquid or of the shop's かえし. Pork, so not vegan.

items.ja: ★十六代真っ赤卵使用　卵かけご飯
items.en: Egg-over-rice made with 十六代真っ赤卵 — a branded egg with an unusually deep red-orange yolk, cracked raw over hot rice. Starred (★) on the option screen
items.section: 追加トッピング Add-on options (10個まで選択)
items.note: Rice and a raw egg are both wheat-free in themselves, which is why this looks like the safe order — but tamago-kake gohan is defined by the soy sauce you pour on it, and the only seasoning this shop puts on the counter is かえし, neat soy tare. Ask whether it arrives pre-seasoned and whether any dashi-shoyu is used; if it can be served naked, the rice and egg themselves are clear. Raw egg, so not vegan.

items.en: A bowl of plain white rice. Starred (★) on the option screen. Ordered as an add-on alongside a bowl, not on its own
items.section: 追加トッピング Add-on options (10個まで選択)
items.note: Plain steamed gohan is the one genuinely wheat-free thing in a ramen shop — no soy, no tare, no noodle. It stays 'ask' rather than 'gf' for two reasons that are real rather than theoretical: this is a 12-seat counter where the only other thing being handled is wheat noodles, and the かえし bottle on the table is what most customers immediately tip into it. Order it undressed, keep it away from the tare, and it is rice and water. Vegan as served plain — but confirm nothing is drizzled on it.

items.ja: 薄切りチャーシュー2枚
items.en: Two extra thin-sliced chashu, added to any bowl from the option screen
items.section: 追加トッピング Add-on options (10個まで選択)
items.note: Chashu is pork simmered in a soy-sauce braise, so it carries wheat in its own right regardless of what it goes on. Not vegan.

items.ja: 厚切りチャーシュー1枚
items.en: One extra thick-cut chashu slab — the same piece that comes as the single luxury slice on the ¥1,800 チャーシューラーメン
items.section: 追加トッピング Add-on options (10個まで選択)
items.note: Soy-braised pork. Wheat via the braising soy sauce; not vegan.

items.en: A soft-centred seasoned egg — the same one that comes as standard in the ¥1,500 特製ラーメン
items.section: 追加トッピング Add-on options (10個まで選択)
items.note: The clue is in 煮 — this egg has been steeped in a soy-sauce marinade, which is exactly how a boiled egg that ought to be safe becomes a wheat item. Egg, so not vegan. If you want an unseasoned egg, the 生卵 line below is the raw one.

items.en: Garlic chives, added as a topping — a Sapporo-miso-lineage garnish that fits this bowl's stir-fried moyashi-and-mince character
items.section: 追加トッピング Add-on options (10個まで選択)
items.note: A green vegetable, and if it arrives plain (raw or blanched) it is wheat-free and vegan. But a ramen counter's ニラ topping is very often ニラだれ — chives steeped in a soy-and-sesame marinade — and this shop publishes nothing about which it serves. Both flags stay 'ask' until someone at the counter says whether it is dressed.

items.en: A raw egg — the same branded 十六代真っ赤卵 as the rice bowl above — to break over your ramen or your rice. The cheapest add-on on the machine
items.section: 追加トッピング Add-on options (10個まで選択)
items.note: An egg in its shell carries no wheat, and unlike the 半熟煮卵 it has not been sat in a soy marinade — so this is the one egg on the machine that is not itself a soy-sauce item. It is only 'ask' rather than 'gf' because of where it lands: it is served to be cracked into a wheat-noodle bowl, and the shop makes no allergen statement. Egg, so never vegan.

items.en: Black oolong tea, sold cold from the option screen — the only soft drink the machine offers
items.section: 追加トッピング Add-on options (10個まで選択)
items.note: Oolong is a tea leaf and contains no grain at all — importantly, this is NOT 麦茶, which is roasted barley and would be a straightforward gluten problem. The flag stays 'ask' only because the machine names no brand or product, so what actually lands on the counter is unverified. As a plain tea it involves no animal product, so vegan.

items.ja: からだを想うオールフリー
items.en: Suntory's "All-Free" — an alcohol-free, calorie-free beer-taste drink, in the health-claim (トクホ-style) version. The one grown-up drink on the machine, and the most expensive add-on after the chashu bowl
items.section: 追加トッピング Add-on options (10個まで選択)
items.note: READ THIS ONE TWICE. "Alcohol-free" is not "gluten-free": an All-Free is brewed from 麦芽 — barley malt — exactly like the beer it imitates, and barley is a gluten grain. It is also one of the few gluten sources in Japan that is NOT on the statutory allergen labelling list, so it will not show up on any 特定原材料 line; barley is simply not required to be declared. A traveller reaching for the non-alcoholic option specifically because they are being careful is reaching for the wrong thing. Vegan left at 'ask' — malt and hops are plant matter but the shop names no ingredient list.

items.ja: テイクアウト冷凍ラーメン
items.en: Take-home frozen ramen kit, flagged 販売開始 ("now on sale") in a red box across the bottom of the ticket-machine screen with its own 注文 button. No price is shown on the screen
items.note: Price deliberately left blank: the machine's takeaway panel carries no legible figure in any photograph I could read, and inventing one would be worse than leaving it. Ask at the counter. Contents are the shop's own soy ramen — wheat noodle and soy tare — so the diet flags follow the bowl. Worth knowing that a frozen retail pack, unlike the counter, is legally obliged to carry an ingredient and allergen panel, so this is the one item here whose 小麦 line you can actually read for yourself.

items.en: Kaeshi — the shop's own soy tare concentrate, free on the table. The 卓上調味料のお楽しみ方 card tells you when to use it: 味をもう少し濃くしたい時や、キレ・パンチを加えたい時に。少しずつ加えながらお好みのバランスでお楽しみください — add it a little at a time when you want the bowl darker or sharper
items.note: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT LINE ON THIS PAGE FOR A WHEAT-AVOIDING READER. Kaeshi is the soy-sauce base a ramen tare is built from — soy sauce reduced with mirin and sugar — and Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat by default. It is sitting in an unlabelled bottle on a 12-seat counter where it will get poured, splashed and passed hand to hand, so it is a contamination source as well as an ingredient: it is why the plain rice above is 'ask' rather than 'gf'. Vegan is 'ask' because a ramen kaeshi is often built out with katsuobushi or niboshi, and the shop states nothing.

items.en: Niboshi vinegar — dried-sardine-infused vinegar, free on the table. The shop's card: 味をさっぱり整えたい時におすすめです。後半に加えることで、まろやかさと煮干しの香り・旨みがより引き立ちます — add it late in the bowl to lift the sardine aroma and round the whole thing off
items.note: 煮干し is dried baby sardine, so this is fish and never vegan — which is not obvious from the word 'vinegar' and is worth flagging to anyone scanning a table for something harmless. On gluten it is 'ask' rather than 'no': rice vinegar itself is wheat-free, but ramen-shop niboshi vinegars are frequently cut with soy sauce, and the shop lists no ingredients.

items.en: Ground red chilli, single-ingredient (一味 = one flavour, as against 七味 which is a seven-spice blend). Free on the table. The card: 辛味がお好きな方に。すっきりとした辛さで、ラーメンの風味を損なわず心地よい刺激を加えます
items.note: 一味 is nothing but dried chilli, so as a product it is wheat-free and plant-only — genuinely useful to know, because its cousin 七味 sometimes carries other additions. 'Ask' rather than 'gf' purely because it is a shared shaker on a counter of wheat noodles, handled by people who have just been eating them.

items.en: White pepper, free on the table — and the shop makes a point of it: チーホーの一杯と相性抜群。豚骨ベースのスープに、どこか懐かしい香りと程よいスパイス感をプラスします. That line is also the shop's own confirmation that the broth is 豚骨ベース, pork-bone based
items.note: Ground white pepper is a single spice — no wheat, no animal product. Left at 'ask' for gluten only because of the shared shaker on a wheat counter. Note the incidental value of this card: it is the shop stating in its own words that the soup is pork-bone based, which settles the vegan question for every bowl above without needing a review to tell you.

tokyo_wonder_kebab_hikarie_mae.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. THE SHOP'S OWN SITE IS DEAD: wonderkebab-hikariemae.com no longer resolves at all — DNS returns nothing for the bare domain or www, on http or https — and the Wayback Machine holds only a 2021-12-31 redirect and a robots.txt for it, no page content. The record's `website` field is therefore a dead link and should be treated as one. What replaces it is better than an aggregator: the stand's OWN painted A-boards, photographed at full resolution and readable end to end. THE PRICE IS A SINGLE FLAT NUMBER AND IT HAS JUST MOVED. The board reads Chicken(チキン), Beff(ビーフ), Mix(ミックス) — ALL ¥800円, and the ¥800 is a white sticker pasted over the previous figure inside a yellow patch, i.e. this shop re-prices by covering the old number. Photographs date the moves exactly: the board read ALL 700円 in 2025/03 (a reviewer's caption that month simply says 値上げしてた, 'they've put the prices up'), still 700円 in 2025/05, 2026/01 and 2026/02, and reads ¥800 in the 2026/08 shot. A 2026/08 diner writes ・ケバブ（ラップ）¥800, matching the current board exactly; a 2025/08 diner paid 700円, a 2024/03 diner 600円, and a long-time regular remembers 500円. So use ¥800 and distrust any older figure you find elsewhere — including this shop's own Tabelog 料理 menu, which is a 公式 shop registration but carries 更新日 2021/10/11 and still lists the long-abandoned split pricing (チキン/MIX サンド 500円, ビーフ 800円, ラップ/ライス チキン 600円). Those 2021 numbers are quoted below only inside notes, never as a price. FORMAT, NOT DISH, IS WHAT YOU CHOOSE: the same carved doner goes into four things at the same ¥800 — SANDO (pita), WRAP (tortilla), DON (over rice) and TSUMAMI (on salad, no bread at all) — and then you pick a sauce. 東京都渋谷区渋谷2-22-13, 172m from Shibuya Station, immediately next to the Gindaco takoyaki stand and across from Hikarie; 08:00-23:00 every day except the New Year break 12/27-1/5; 2 seats, so this is a standing takeaway window; CASH ONLY (no cards, no e-money); no reservations; takeout and delivery. Tel 03-3498-8183. Tabelog's budget band is ~¥999 for both lunch and dinner. There is a sister stand, ワンダーケバブ 道玄坂店 at 渋谷区道玄坂2-10-2 — different listing, prices not evidenced here, do not carry these across. The shop's own PR line says it had been at Hikarie-mae for eight years as of that writing. THERE IS NO ALLERGEN CHART, no ingredient list and no gluten-free or vegetarian claim anywhere — but two shop-sourced physical details do real work below: a delivery carton stacked at the stand in 2025/05 is printed 「おいしいフラワートルティーヤ 10インチ」, a 10-inch FLOUR tortilla, which settles what the WRAP is made of; and a 業務用 case of Kagome tomato ketchup, 1kg x 12, sits beside the board in 2026/01. The boards also carry hand-made FREE PALESTINE and STOP THE KILLING placards taped over the artwork, which is simply what the stand looks like at present.

items.ja: ケバブサンド (SANDO / サンド)
items.en: Kebab Sando — carved doner stuffed into a split pita-style flatbread with lettuce, tomato and red onion, plus your chosen sauce. The board's top photo and the shop's most-ordered format. Same ¥800 whichever meat you pick
items.section: ケバブ Kebab — ALL ¥800 (choose meat, format and sauce)
items.note: The bread is the whole problem: a pita is wheat flour, and a Turkish stand's pide/pita is not made any other way. A 2024 diner guessed from the flavour that it might be 全粒粉 (wholemeal) — which, if true, is still wheat, just browner. Doner meat, so not vegan. If you need to be off bread, the DON and TSUMAMI formats below are the same meat without any, but read their notes before assuming they are clear.

items.ja: ケバブラップ (WRAP / ラップ)
items.en: Kebab Wrap — the same meat and salad rolled in a large soft flatbread and wrapped in foil to eat standing up. The biggest of the four by volume; 2026 diners repeatedly describe it as packed solid. ¥800, confirmed by a 2026/08 diner's own note ・ケバブ（ラップ）¥800
items.section: ケバブ Kebab — ALL ¥800 (choose meat, format and sauce)
items.note: This one is not an inference. A delivery carton photographed at the stand is printed 「おいしいフラワートルティーヤ 10インチ」 — a 10-inch FLOUR tortilla, i.e. wheat, straight from the shop's own stock. So the wrapper is wheat and the shop is not using a corn tortilla. Doner meat, so not vegan.

items.en: Kebab Don — the carved meat piled over rice in a bowl with the same salad and sauce, no bread involved. On the older Tabelog registration this format was called ケバブライス. A 2025/05 diner says the man at the window recommended it over the wrap and it was enormous; a 2024 diner singles out the seasoning of the rice underneath as the best part
items.section: ケバブ Kebab — ALL ¥800 (choose meat, format and sauce)
items.note: One of only two bread-free formats here, so it is the obvious question to ask — but do not assume it is clear. Three unknowns stack up. (1) The rice is SEASONED, not plain: a diner specifically praises 丼の下にあるごはんの味付け, so this is a flavoured pilaf-style base, not white gohan, and nothing states what it is flavoured with. (2) The doner marinade is undeclared, and a Japanese kebab stand's marinade very often reaches for soy sauce. (3) The sauces are undeclared and this shop's own 2021 menu listed a 照り焼き (teriyaki) sauce, which is soy sauce by definition — evidence that soy is or was on this counter. Add that it is a two-seat window where the same tongs and the same board handle pita and tortilla all day, and 'ask' is as far as this can honestly go. Meat, so not vegan.

items.ja: ケバブつまみ (TSUMAMI / つまみ)
items.en: Kebab Tsumami — 'a nibble': the carved meat plated on a bed of shredded cabbage and leaf salad with tomato, no bread and no rice, meant to be picked at with a drink. A 2025/03 diner describes it as the already-carved meat re-tossed in the pan and plated
items.section: ケバブ Kebab — ALL ¥800 (choose meat, format and sauce)
items.note: The nearest thing to a wheat-free order in the building — meat and raw vegetables and nothing else structural — which is exactly why it needs the caveats spelled out rather than waved through. The marinade on the doner cone is undeclared; the sauce is undeclared; the same small counter is covered in pita and flour tortilla; and there is no allergen information of any kind. Worth asking for it with no sauce. Meat, so not vegan.

items.en: Chicken doner — one of the three meats, chosen at the window. No surcharge: the board's ALL ¥800 covers every meat in every format. Historically the cheapest option (the 2021 registration priced a chicken sando at 500円 against 800円 for beef); that split is gone
items.section: 肉を選ぶ Choose your meat (no surcharge)
items.note: Price left blank on purpose — this is a choice inside the ¥800, not a separately priced line. Doner chicken is marinated before it goes on the cone and the marinade is not published; Japanese kebab stands commonly build one on soy sauce, and this shop has offered a teriyaki sauce in the past. Chicken, so never vegan.

items.en: Beef doner — spelled "Beff" on the shop's own board. Included in the flat ¥800; under the old 2021 pricing beef was the premium meat at 800円 while chicken was 500-600円, so the flat price is effectively a beef price for everyone
items.section: 肉を選ぶ Choose your meat (no surcharge)
items.note: A choice inside the ¥800, hence no price of its own. Same unpublished marinade question as the chicken. Beef, so never vegan.

items.ja: ミックス (Mix / ミックス)
items.en: Mix — both meats together, the option 2026 diners order most often. Included in the flat ¥800
items.section: 肉を選ぶ Choose your meat (no surcharge)
items.note: A choice inside the ¥800. Two undeclared marinades instead of one. Not vegan.

items.en: Mild sauce — the shop's own board glosses it 辛くない, 'not spicy'. One of three on the SAUSE (sic) panel that stands beside the main board
items.note: No charge, hence no price. The sauce is the least visible and most likely wheat carrier on this stand: nothing about its composition is published, and the shop's own 2021 Tabelog registration listed a 照り焼き (teriyaki) sauce among six choices — teriyaki is soy sauce, sugar and mirin, so soy sauce has been on this counter. The current board shows only three sauces (MILD / MIX / HOT); the older six-choice list (甘口, ピリ辛, 辛口, ヨーグルト, 照り焼き, 激辛) is quoted here as history, not as something you can order today. Vegan is 'ask' because that same old list included a ヨーグルト (yoghurt) sauce, i.e. dairy has also been on this counter, and mild kebab sauces are frequently yoghurt- or mayonnaise-based.

items.en: Mix sauce — glossed ピリ辛, mildly hot; the middle setting, and what most reviewers pick. A 2026/04 diner describes the three levels as 甘口・中辛・辛口, another says the ピリ辛 was not hot at all to them
items.note: Included, so no price. 'Mix' here means mild and hot blended, not a separate recipe — so it inherits every unknown of both. No ingredient list, no allergen line; see the MILD note for why soy sauce and dairy are both live possibilities on this counter.

items.en: Hot sauce — glossed 辛口. The spiciest of the three now on the board; the shop's older menu went one step further with a 激辛 that is no longer listed
items.note: Included, so no price. Same undeclared composition as the other two. If you are avoiding wheat, the useful move at this window is to ask for the meat with no sauce at all rather than to pick between three unknowns.

items.en: Extra meat — an upsize on the doner in any format. It exists as a line on the shop's own Tabelog registration but does not appear on any current board photograph, so whether it survived the move to flat pricing is unclear
items.note: NO PRICE RECORDED, deliberately. The only figures that exist for this are on the shop's 2021 registration — ビーフ ＋300円, チキン・MIX ＋200円 — and that registration also still shows the abandoned 500/600/800 split pricing, so its numbers are demonstrably five years out of date and quoting them as current would be worse than leaving the field empty. Ask at the window. Diet flags follow the meat: undeclared marinade, and never vegan.

tokyo_woodberry_bakery.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Tax-included figures transcribed from the shop's OWN branch menu PDFs, linked from woodberrycoffee.com/pages/menu under the BAKERY heading: 260805_BAKERY_FOOD.pdf (file dated 2026-08-05) and 2608_BAKERY_DRINK.pdf. Both were cross-checked against photographs of the physical card on the table and the counter board, shot 2026-03 and 2026-04, and every overlapping price agrees, which is why the confidence is high. THE SHOP'S OWN PDF DISAGREES WITH ITSELF, and this record follows the newer figure: its first page (a summary sheet carrying the morning set) prices エッグベネディクト and アボカドトースト at ¥1,870 and the acai bowl at ¥1,960, while the booklet pages behind it and both in-store photographs say ¥1,970, ¥1,970 and ¥1,980. クロックマダム ¥1,670 appears ONLY on that stale-looking summary page and on neither counter card — treat it as the least reliable line here. TWO ITEMS COME FROM THE IN-STORE CARD AND NOT THE PDF: 季節のクレープ ¥1,980 and the 季節のスープとパンのセット ¥1,320 were on the counter board photographed 2026-03; the seasonal slots rotate (the 2026-04 booklet's seasonal crepe was フォレ・ノワール; the current PDF replaces the slot with ティラミスフレンチトースト ¥1,650), and the grilled tuna sandwich's vegetable changed from asparagus in April to 菜の花 on the current sheet. The ハンドドリップ line is on the in-store card with 「PLEASE ASK US」 where the price should be, so it is recorded with no price rather than a guess. THE BAKERY-COUNTER PASTRIES ARE A DIFFERENT VINTAGE AND ARE MARKED AS SUCH: the four 焼き菓子 with prices (¥770 × 3, ¥460) come from the shop's own opening announcement, which stamps them 「2024年5月20日現在」. The case rotates; those four are recorded because they are the only ones the shop has ever described in writing, and because one of them carries the gluten-free claim. GLUTEN, PLAINLY: this is a BAKERY. The house bread is 自家製天然酵母と国産有機小麦のカンパーニュ and, per the shop, 有機小麦とライ麦と古代小麦のスペルト全粒粉 — wheat, rye and spelt — plus bagels and shokupan. Every sandwich, toast, lunch plate and french toast is built on it. NOTHING on this record is flagged ‘gf’, including the tarte tatin the shop itself calls ヴィーガン＆グルテンフリー and the 米粉 florentine: those are recipe claims made inside a working wheat bakery, and the shop makes no separate-equipment, separate-room or no-contamination claim anywhere on its site. The honest label for a coeliac is ‘ask, and show a coeliac card’. VEGAN, BY CONTRAST, IS GENUINELY WELL SERVED and the shop says so itself: the concept line on its own location page is 「地球にも身体にも優しいがコンセプトのベーカリー。ヴィーガンやグルテンフリーなどのヘルスコンシャスなレシピの焼き菓子とパンをご提供するベーカリーカフェです」. There is a named vegan sandwich, a vegan crepe, vegan ice cream, an all-plant acai bowl, and soy (+¥50) or oat (+¥100) milk on every espresso drink. The shop publishes NO allergen chart — no アレルギー or 特定原材料 page exists on the site, and the FAQ does not mention allergens — so every flag here is reasoned from the ingredient lines the shop prints under each dish, and those lines are summaries, not full recipes. Hours are 9:00–18:00 with 定休日あり (LO food 17:00, drink 18:00) per the shop's location page; the morning set is 9:00–11:00 only. The 2024 opening announcement's 11:00–18:00 is out of date. Address confirmed 東京都渋谷区東2-18-7 on both the shop's site and Tabelog — the same Higashi 2-chome block as WOODBERRY COFFEE 渋谷店 (2-20-18), which is a DIFFERENT shop with a different menu; do not merge them. Tabelog has no registered menu for this listing (the /dtlmenu/ URL falls through to the shop top page).

items.ja: ベーカリーモーニングセット
items.en: Morning set, 9:00–11:00 only — three recommended breads, seasonal salad, almond butter and homemade jam, plus a set drink
items.section: BAKERY MORNING SET モーニングセット (9:00–11:00)
items.note: Printed [9:00-11:00] on the shop's own PDF, so it is off the card by mid-morning. The bakery's bread is WHEAT and then some: the shop's own copy reads 「自家製天然酵母と国産（有機）小麦で作るベーグル・カンパーニュブレッド」, and its opening announcement says the campagne is 「有機小麦と、ライ麦、古代小麦のスペルト全粒粉を使ったカンパーニュ」 — wheat, RYE and SPELT, three gluten grains in one loaf. Vegan is 'ask' rather than 'no': nothing in the printed components (bread, seasonal salad, almond butter, homemade jam) is named as dairy or egg, but the shop does not state what dresses the salad, whether butter is served with the bread, or what is in the jam, and the set drink defaults to dairy milk unless you ask for soy (+¥50) or oat (+¥100). Cross-contamination: this is a working bakery that mills, weighs and proves organic wheat, rye and spelt dough in the same room, and the same counter that plates the gluten-free items. The shop makes no dedicated-facility or separate-equipment claim anywhere on its site.

items.en: Assortment of three recommended breads (part of the morning set)
items.section: BAKERY MORNING SET モーニングセット (9:00–11:00)
items.note: A component of the ¥1,650 morning set, not separately priced on the card. items.section: BAKERY MORNING SET モーニングセット (9:00–11:00)
items.note: A component of the ¥1,650 morning set; also sold as a ¥440 side. The shop does not print the dressing, and a Japanese house dressing is very often soy-sauce based, i.e. wheat. Ask. Cross-contamination: this is a working bakery that mills, weighs and proves organic wheat, rye and spelt dough in the same room, and the same counter that plates the gluten-free items. The shop makes no dedicated-facility or separate-equipment claim anywhere on its site.

items.en: Set drink — choose one of: today's coffee / cafe latte / long black / homemade ginger ale / homemade lemonade / Yakushima teas

items.note: Included in the morning set and in the ¥2,750 lunch set. Of the six choices the black coffee, the long black, the ginger ale, the lemonade and the plain Yakushima tea are the plant-based ones; the cafe latte is dairy unless you ask for soy (+¥50) or oat (+¥100).

items.en: Eggs Benedict on house campagne — bacon or smoked salmon, hollandaise, kale
items.section: OPEN SANDWICH オープンサンド
items.note: Shop's ingredient line: カンパーニュブレッド, ベーコンまたはスモークサーモン, オランデーズソース, ケール. The bakery's bread is WHEAT and then some: the shop's own copy reads 「自家製天然酵母と国産（有機）小麦で作るベーグル・カンパーニュブレッド」, and its opening announcement says the campagne is 「有機小麦と、ライ麦、古代小麦のスペルト全粒粉を使ったカンパーニュ」 — wheat, RYE and SPELT, three gluten grains in one loaf. Hollandaise is egg yolk and butter, so this is out for both diets. NOTE THE PRICE: ¥1,970 is what the OPEN SANDWICH page of the shop's current (2026-08-05) PDF prints and what the in-store card photographed 2026-03 and 2026-04 shows; the summary page of the same PDF still reads ¥1,870.

items.en: Avocado toast on house campagne — avocado, egg, lemon, cream cheese
items.section: OPEN SANDWICH オープンサンド
items.note: Shop's ingredient line: カンパーニュブレッド, アボカド, エッグ, レモン, クリームチーズ — egg and cream cheese, so not vegan even before the bread. The bakery's bread is WHEAT and then some: the shop's own copy reads 「自家製天然酵母と国産（有機）小麦で作るベーグル・カンパーニュブレッド」, and its opening announcement says the campagne is 「有機小麦と、ライ麦、古代小麦のスペルト全粒粉を使ったカンパーニュ」 — wheat, RYE and SPELT, three gluten grains in one loaf. Same ¥1,870/¥1,970 discrepancy between the two pages of the shop's own PDF as the Benedict; the in-store card says ¥1,970.

items.note: From the shop's own opening announcement on woodberrycoffee.com, which stamps the four pastries 「(2024年5月20日現在)」 — i.e. these are the four it chose to describe when the bakery opened, with prices as of May 2024. The pastry case rotates and the prices are two years old; read them as evidence of what this bakery makes, not as today's card. The shop's words: 鹿児島・屋久島八万寿茶園の緑茶を使用し、カシューナッツベースの濃厚なムースとバニラのまろやかなムースの2層、「砂糖を使わずメープルシロップのみで甘さをつけたシュガーフリーのレシピ」. A cashew-based raw cake is normally both dairy-free and flour-free, but the shop says neither ヴィーガン nor グルテンフリー for this one where it says both for its neighbours on the same page — that silence is exactly why this is 'ask' twice. Cross-contamination: this is a working bakery that mills, weighs and proves organic wheat, rye and spelt dough in the same room, and the same counter that plates the gluten-free items. The shop makes no dedicated-facility or separate-equipment claim anywhere on its site.

items.note: From the shop's own opening announcement on woodberrycoffee.com, which stamps the four pastries 「(2024年5月20日現在)」 — i.e. these are the four it chose to describe when the bakery opened, with prices as of May 2024. The pastry case rotates and the prices are two years old; read them as evidence of what this bakery makes, not as today's card. THIS IS THE ONE A COELIAC WILL ASK ABOUT. The shop's own words: 「紅玉りんごを丸々１つ使ったヴィーガン＆グルテンフリーのタルトタタン。カスタードにはサツマイモを使用しており、お腹にも優しい甘さになっています。クッキー生地にはアールグレイを練り込み」. Vegan is recorded as the shop states it. GLUTEN IS STILL 'ask', deliberately: the claim is about the RECIPE, not the FACILITY. Cross-contamination: this is a working bakery that mills, weighs and proves organic wheat, rye and spelt dough in the same room, and the same counter that plates the gluten-free items. The shop makes no dedicated-facility or separate-equipment claim anywhere on its site. A recipe-level gluten-free claim from a bakery whose main product is a wheat-rye-spelt sourdough is not a safe answer for coeliac disease — show the kitchen a coeliac card and ask where it is baked, cooled and cut. Also note the shop has not restated the claim since 2024.

A RICE-FLOUR BASE IS NOT A GLUTEN-FREE CLAIM — this is the trap that has caught three 米粉 bakeries already in this project (PUKKU, Sakura Pan Kobo, Conconto), all of which list 小麦 on their own allergen line because wheat is baked in the same workshop. The shop calls the tarte tatin gluten-free and does NOT say it here. Vegan is 'ask' too: a florentine is classically bound with butter and cream and the shop does not say this one is not. Cross-contamination: this is a working bakery that mills, weighs and proves organic wheat, rye and spelt dough in the same room, and the same counter that plates the gluten-free items. The shop makes no dedicated-facility or separate-equipment claim anywhere on its site.

tokyo_ramen_kamo_to_negi_shibu.price_note: Prices not published. The chain's own site names its dishes but lists no prices, its Shibuya branch page carries no menu, and the Tabelog menu tab is empty ("Set menu (0)"). Tabelog puts a visit in the JPY 1,000–1,999 band.

items.en: Duck ramen — the house bowl, built on a duck-and-negi broth
items.note: NOT gluten-free, on the shop's own description twice over. The noodles are 「国産全粒粉と小麦をブレンドした」 — a domestic wholemeal and wheat blend. The tare is built on 濃口生醬油, 淡口醤油 and 再仕込み醤油, all soy sauces, which are wheat-brewed by default in Japan. Worth knowing for a different reason: the DASHI itself is 「鴨・葱・水」のみ — duck, spring onion and water only — so the broth base carries no soy, and it is the tare and noodles that rule it out. Duck makes it non-vegan regardless.

items.en: "Drinkable" oyakodon — chicken and egg over rice, the egg set for only ten seconds so it stays liquid
items.note: The shop states 「火入れは10秒」 for this dish. Chicken and egg rule out vegan. GF is "ask" and leans no: oyakodon is simmered in a soy-and-mirin broth as standard, and this kitchen's documented tare is three kinds of soy sauce, but the shop does not publish this dish's seasoning separately.

tokyo_tokutaro.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. The shop's own site (tokutarou.shop) returns 403 to any non-browser request and Tabelog carries no menu listing, so prices are from a June 2025 Tokyo Shimbun feature; the 2014 All About piece quotes an older 135 yen for the same item.

items.en: Kintsuba — simmered Hokkaido azuki set with agar, cut into a square, coated in a thin batter and griddled on all six faces. The shop's signature; reportedly ~1,000 sold a day.
items.note: NOT gluten-free: the coating batter is 小麦粉 (wheat flour), stated outright in the All About ingredient list (小豆・寒天・小麦粉・塩). Vegan is "ask" rather than yes — the bean paste is finished with 水飴, and Japanese 水飴 is sometimes 麦芽水飴 (barley malt), which would also be a second gluten route; no allergen statement is published either way.

items.en: Bean daifuku — glutinous rice cake with whole beans and azuki paste
items.note: Daifuku is glutinous RICE, not wheat, so the dish itself is plausibly gluten-free — but this is a small shop whose signature product is coated in wheat flour daily, and no allergen or separation statement is published. Ask before assuming.

items.en: Butter dorayaki — azuki and butter between two pancakes
items.note: Dorayaki pancakes are a wheat-flour batter, and this version adds butter, so it fails both diets on its own terms.

items.note: Listed as a product in the 2014 All About piece with no price and no ingredient breakdown. Yōkan is normally azuki, sugar and agar — plant-only and wheat-free — but that is the general recipe, not this shop's stated one.
