items.en: Yukuri set — house amazake-fruit aperitif; small dishes of dried-daikon salad with crab stick and mizuna, sweetcorn chawanmushi with edamame, fried aubergine and bitter melon simmered in miso; a choice of fish (miso-marinated black cod with a dairy sauce, or oil-grilled sea bream and fried fig in a black-vinegar ankake) or meat (deep-fried Japanese pork kakuni with summer vegetables and sesame sauce); sashimi; Niigata Gensen rice, house-blend miso soup and pickles
items.note: Not gluten-free. 銀鱈西京焼 is a 西京味噌 marinade and miso is frequently 麦味噌 (barley); the alternative main is 揚げ (deep-fried) and finished with 黒酢餡掛け and 胡麻だれ, both normally soy-based. かにかま is surimi, which usually carries wheat starch. Not vegan: fish, pork, egg in the chawanmushi, and the miso soup dashi is undeclared.

items.en: Haconiwa kaiseki — octopus simmered soft in a summer-vegetable aspic; a masu box of dried-daikon salad, sweetcorn kuzu jelly, bitter melon in miso with konjac, summer duck with plum and apple, ayu confit, cream cheese with shutou, junsai in mozuku vinegar, deep-fried grapes and quail egg; sashimi; the house noppei simmer; pike conger and aubergine tempura served agedashi-style; hand-cut soba; dessert
items.note: Not gluten-free, twice over and explicitly: the course includes 天麩羅 (a wheat batter, served 揚げ出汁風 in a soy-based broth) and 手打ち蕎麦 — Japanese soba is wheat-blended unless stated 十割, and even then it is dusted with 打ち粉 and boiled in shared water. Not vegan: octopus, duck, ayu, cream cheese, 酒盗 (fermented fish gut) and egg.

items.en: Hana kaiseki — appetisers of summer duck with plum and apple, ayu confit, cream cheese with shutou, junsai, fried grapes and quail egg; a clear summer soup with sweetcorn kuzu jelly, crab shinjo and flower spike; sashimi; miso-marinated black cod with a dairy sauce; the house noppei simmer; chilled soup with mugi-tororo rice and pickles; dessert
items.note: CONTAINS BARLEY, and this is the trap worth naming: the rice course is 麦とろろ御飯 — 麦 is barley, a gluten grain, and barley is NOT on Japan's statutory allergen list, so it will not appear on any allergen table. Also 西京焼 (miso, often barley miso) and 真丈, which commonly binds with egg white and sometimes flour. Not vegan: duck, ayu, crab, fish, dairy and egg.

tokyo_bazoku_asakusa_chugoku_t.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. The shop publishes exactly ONE item to Tabelog and has no site of its own, so this is a fraction of a board that certainly runs longer. Recorded as partial rather than padded out from the shop's category tags.

items.en: Ramen — the shop's hand-pulled noodles, described by the shop as chewy and handmade
items.note: 手打拉麺 means hand-pulled wheat noodles — the pulling is what develops the gluten, so the technique the shop is named for is the reason it is not gluten-free. Chinese-style ramen broth is normally pork- and soy-based.

tokyo_shokudo_naganoya.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Only ONE item is published to Tabelog, though the listing carries 742 photos and the shop is categorised for teishoku, katsudon and curry — so the real board is much longer. Recorded as partial; the rest is not guessed at.

items.en: Pork cutlet curry rice
items.note: Wheat twice over, and both halves are easy to miss. The カツ is crumbed in パン粉 (breadcrumb) and usually floured before the egg wash; and Japanese curry is built on a ROUX of wheat flour and fat, which is what separates it from the soup curry and Indian styles. Pork and egg rule out vegan.

tokyo_tsukemen_zuppa_suidobash.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Tabelog carries no menu at all (0 items across every section), so the board comes from Vegewel, cross-checked against a first-hand visit write-up rather than taken on Vegewel alone — this project does not rest a vegan claim on a single directory. The two disagree on price: Vegewel lists the soy-meat miso ramen at ¥900, the visit (Dec 2022) records ¥880+¥100. Vegewel's figures are used as the more recent. The shop also states 五葷抜き (allium-free) is available for oriental-vegan diners.

items.en: Tsukemen — dipping noodles, the house dish
items.note: NOT gluten-free: tsukemen, ramen and tantanmen noodles are wheat. Being vegan changes nothing about that — this shop is a find for a vegan and a dead end for a coeliac, and a coeliac vegan cannot eat the noodle dishes at all. Vegan ON REQUEST, not by default: the shop's own line, reported first-hand, is 「つけ麺・ラーメンはヴィーガン対応可能です」 — buy the ticket and tell staff you want it vegan. Do not assume the default build is plant-based. The visiting writer reports the soup as 「No meat nor fish used to make the soup. Vegetable only.」 — a first-hand account of the broth, which is the claim that matters most here, since ramen broth is where animal stock normally hides.

items.en: Soy-milk tantanmen

ONLY THE DESSERT AND FRENCH-TOAST SECTIONS ARE RECORDED HERE: the bar/dinner PDF interleaves its columns when the text is extracted, so item, price and allergen cannot be paired reliably — and mis-pairing an allergen label on a coeliac app is worse than omitting it. items.en: Panna Cotta
items.note: The best coeliac prospect on this board, and on the restaurant's own declaration rather than a guess: its allergen label reads ( Milk / 乳 ) ALONE — no wheat, no egg. Panna cotta is cream, sugar and gelatin, so there is no plausible barley route either. Read from the hotel's own allergen-labelled menu. Two limits on any such label in Japan: it covers the statutory allergens, which include 小麦 (wheat) but NOT 大麦 (barley), and it says nothing about shared equipment. Milk and gelatin rule out vegan.

tokyo_bakery_santino_shibuya.price_note: ⚠⚠ READ THIS BEFORE THE PRICES. This is a 米粉パン専門店 — a RICE-FLOUR bread specialist — and it is NOT gluten-free. Two independent visitors on the shop's Tabelog page record the composition and the allergen labels, and both point the same way: 「全ての商品が米粉90%、小麦グルテン10%の割合」, and the shop's own product labels are transcribed as 特定原材料：小麦・乳・大豆・りんご and 特定原材料：小麦・乳 — 小麦 (WHEAT) declared first in both. A third visitor calls the shop 「ほぼ、グルテンフリー！」 ("almost gluten-free!"), which is precisely the misreading this record exists to prevent: "rice flour bakery" reads as safe and this one is not. Tabelog carries no menu, so the products and prices below come from those visitor write-ups rather than from the shop, hence provisional. The shop's own domain (takewaka.co.jp) NO LONGER RESOLVES — dead, worth feeding to the hijacked/dead-domain checker. Not closed, though: Tabelog lists it trading 10:00–21:00 daily at 渋谷スクランブルスクエア 1F.

Wheat gluten is the exact protein a coeliac reacts to; a 10% inclusion is not a trace, it is an ingredient. This item's own label is transcribed as 特定原材料：小麦・乳・大豆・りんご — wheat, milk, soy and apple. tokyo_hanuri_shibuya_honten.price_note: Prices approximate — may change; tax included as listed. The shop's own site shows only four featured dishes and hands the full board to Retty, which is where this came from. THE FOOD MENU IS RECORDED; THE DRINKS LIST IS NOT — it runs past a hundred entries (makgeolli, soju, sours, highballs) and itemising it would bury the food. Two things to carry to the bar instead: BEER IS BARLEY, and 焼酎 may be 麦焼酎, which is barley too. Retty states plainly アレルギー表示：ページ内にアレルギー表示なし — no allergen labelling anywhere on the page, so every note below is inference from the dish, not a declaration from the shop. items.en: Hanger steak

items.ja: お肉のガーリックまみれ
items.en: Beef smothered in garlic
items.note: Garlic and oil carry no wheat, but a garlic dressing at a yakiniku counter is normally built on soy. Undeclared.

items.en: Short rib in a salted-kelp tare
items.note: The name carries タレ. Yakiniku tare is soy-sauce based, and soy sauce is wheat by default. Kelp itself is fine; the sauce is not.

items.en: Griddled lean beef shabu
items.note: Thin beef cooked briefly; the dip is the question and is not stated.

items.en: Fragrant spicy short rib
items.note: A spicy pre-marinated cut — Korean chilli marinades are gochujang and soy, and gochujang is itself commonly made with wheat flour or barley malt.

items.ja: 本日の厳選和牛３種盛り合わせ
items.romaji: honjitsu no gensen wagyū sanshu moriawase
items.en: Today's three selected wagyu cuts
items.note: Cuts change daily and some arrive marinated; ask which of the three.

items.en: Two thick-cut slices of premium salted tongue — from the tan-moto, of which only four or five thick slices come off each tongue
items.note: The shop's own recommendation, and named 塩. A salted cut is the coeliac-friendlier way to order at a yakiniku table — the meat itself is clean and only the dip is not. Nothing is declared here, so confirm the dip.

items.en: Two thick-cut slices of premium skirt — around 2kg comes off each animal
items.note: Thick-cut and grilled at the table; the dip is unstated.

items.en: Two thick-cut slices of premium hanger — only about 1kg comes off each animal
items.note: Dip unstated.

items.en: Thick-cut premium liver, to be cooked through
items.note: The shop asks that it be well grilled. Dip unstated — sesame-and-salt would be clean, soy would not.

items.en: Raw beef heart
items.note: Raw offal is often served with sesame oil and salt; the dressing is not stated.

items.en: Raw beef tongue
items.note: Dressing unstated.

items.en: Three assorted raw beef cuts
items.note: Dressing unstated.

items.en: Top-blade sukiyaki — a cut of which only about 3kg comes off each animal; grilled briefly and coated in the house yolk tare
items.note: Ruled out twice over by its own description. すき焼き is simmered in warishita — soy sauce, mirin and sugar — and the shop directs you to finish it in the 黄身ダレ, which is both a soy-based tare and raw egg.

items.en: Liver ajillo — dipped briefly through garlic oil so it stays plump rather than drying out on the grill
items.note: Genuinely promising: an ajillo is liver, garlic and olive oil, with no structural wheat and no soy in the classic build. Nothing is declared, and Spanish-style ajillo is sometimes served with bread, so ask.

items.en: Wagyu tartare
items.note: Beef tartare is raw meat and seasoning — but tartare is very often served with toast or a crisp, and the seasoning here is unstated. Ask about both.

items.en: Low-temperature-cooked yukke
items.note: Yukke dressing is soy-based and normally carries gochujang as well.

items.en: Large intestine
items.note: Offal at a yakiniku counter is almost always served pre-marinated in a soy-and-miso tare. Yakiniku tare is soy-sauce based, and soy sauce is wheat by default.

items.en: Small intestine
items.note: Yakiniku tare is soy-sauce based, and soy sauce is wheat by default.

items.en: Premium rumen tripe
items.note: Yakiniku tare is soy-sauce based, and soy sauce is wheat by default.

items.en: Liver
items.note: Yakiniku tare is soy-sauce based, and soy sauce is wheat by default.

items.en: Trimmed liver offcuts
items.note: Yakiniku tare is soy-sauce based, and soy sauce is wheat by default.

items.en: Assorted offal
items.note: Yakiniku tare is soy-sauce based, and soy sauce is wheat by default.

items.en: Tripe yukke
items.note: Yukke dressing is soy and gochujang.

items.en: Simmered offal
items.note: Simmered in soy and miso.

items.en: Bean sprout namul
items.note: Namul is blanched vegetable dressed with sesame oil, salt and garlic — plant-only in the classic build and one of the few things here a vegan could eat. Two unstated questions: most kitchens add a little soy sauce, and a yakiniku kitchen may use a dashi or beef stock. Ask both.

items.en: Grilled bamboo shoot namul
items.note: Same two questions as the bean sprout namul.

items.en: Rapeseed-flower namul
items.note: Same two questions.

items.ja: 春キャベツと桜エビのナムル
items.romaji: haru kyabetsu to sakura ebi no namuru
items.en: Spring cabbage and sakura shrimp namul
items.note: Contains sakura shrimp, so not vegan. Same soy question as the other namul.

items.en: New-season onion namul
items.note: Same two questions.

items.ja: 春のナムルの盛り合わせ
items.en: Assorted spring namul
items.note: A mixed plate — if it includes the sakura shrimp namul it is not vegan. Ask what is on it.

items.en: Korean seaweed
items.note: Korean gim is seaweed brushed with sesame oil and salt — plant-only, and one of the very few outright vegan items on this board. Wheat is unlikely but the seasoning is not declared.

items.en: Beef tongue simmered Japanese-style
items.note: 和風 simmering means dashi and soy sauce — wheat from the soy, fish from the dashi.

items.ja: ホタルイカと牛ハツのピリ辛和え
items.romaji: hotaruika to gyū hatsu no pirikara ae
items.en: Firefly squid and beef heart in a spicy dressing
items.note: A spicy Korean-style dressing means gochujang and soy.

items.ja: 和牛タタキと新玉ポン酢
items.en: Seared wagyu tataki with new onion and ponzu
items.note: Ponzu is citrus plus SOY SAUCE, and it is usually made with a bonito dashi as well — wheat and fish in one dressing. A common trap, because ponzu reads as simply citrus.

items.en: Choregi salad
items.note: Leaves in a sesame-oil dressing. Choregi dressing normally contains soy sauce; undeclared.

items.ja: 春キャベツと桜エビのチョレギサラダ
items.romaji: haru kyabetsu to sakura ebi no choregi sarada
items.en: Spring cabbage and sakura shrimp choregi salad
items.note: Sakura shrimp rules out vegan; the dressing question stands.

items.en: Chilled tomato
items.note: Chilled tomato, served plain — with the salad leaves and the seaweed, one of the few genuinely vegan things here. Confirm nothing is dressed on it.

items.ja: 栃木県産ピーマンのまる焼き
items.en: Whole grilled Tochigi green pepper
items.note: A whole pepper on the grill — no wheat and no animal in the vegetable itself. The two questions are whether it is brushed with anything and that it cooks on the same grill as soy-marinated meat.

items.ja: ジャンボマッシュルーム
items.en: Jumbo mushroom
items.note: Grilled mushroom; same two questions as the pepper.

items.en: Jumbo nameko mushroom
items.note: Same two questions.

items.en: Ssam lettuce
items.note: Plain lettuce leaves for wrapping — nothing but the leaf. The only caution is what gets wrapped in it, and that any 味噌 or ssamjang served alongside is a separate order.

items.en: Grilled garlic
items.note: Garlic cloves grilled, usually in oil or foil. Same shared-grill question.

items.en: Napa cabbage kimchi
items.note: Kimchi reads vegan and often is not: Korean kimchi is commonly made with salted fermented seafood, and sometimes with a wheat-flour paste. Neither is declared.

items.en: Mountain yam kimchi
items.note: Same two questions.

items.en: Assorted kimchi
items.note: Same two questions.

items.en: House egg-yolk tare
items.note: Named ダレ, so soy-based, and it is raw egg yolk. Worth settling in one question because this is also the intended dip for the ミスジすき焼き.

items.en: Grated mountain yam with a raw egg
items.note: Grated yam carries no wheat, but tororo is nearly always slackened with dashi or a soy-based tsuyu, and 月見 means a raw egg on top.

items.en: Grated daikon with ponzu
items.note: Ponzu is soy sauce with citrus, usually built on bonito dashi.

items.en: Wakame and egg soup
items.note: Egg, and the broth is a soy-seasoned stock.

items.en: Yukgaejang soup
items.note: Built on beef stock with gochujang and soy.

items.en: Small rice
items.note: Plain white rice. Medium ¥385, large ¥495 — the one thing on this board with no route to either diet.

items.ja: 和牛と春野菜のビビンバ
items.romaji: wagyū to haru yasai no bibinba
items.en: Wagyu and spring vegetable bibimbap
items.note: Bibimbap is dressed with gochujang, which is commonly made with wheat flour or barley malt, and this one has beef in it.

items.en: Yukgaejang gukbap
items.note: The yukgaejang broth over rice — soy and gochujang.

items.en: Naengmyeon
items.note: Korean naengmyeon is normally buckwheat and potato starch rather than wheat, unlike Japanese 冷やし中華 — so it is worth asking rather than assuming. The broth at a yakiniku shop is beef.

tokyo_tokyo_gyoza_stand_oolong.price_note: Prices tax-included as printed by the shop, on a listing marked 公式 — the trading information is published by the restaurant itself. No allergen statement, so the notes below are inference from the dish. ⚠ BE HONEST ABOUT THIS ONE BEFORE WALKING IN: the shop bills itself as ミシュランシェフ考案の餃子とビール — gyoza and beer devised by a Michelin chef — and both halves of that phrase are out for a coeliac. Gyoza wrappers are wheat, the noodles are wheat, and BEER IS BARLEY. Of the twenty dishes on the board only a handful have any route to a gluten-free order, and they are the cold and vegetable dishes rather than anything the shop is known for. A vegan fares slightly better on the vegetable side but the shop is built on pork.

items.en: Fresh zha cai — pickled mustard stem
items.note: One of the few plausible items here for either diet: zha cai is a pickled vegetable. Chinese pickle brines are commonly soy-seasoned and the dressing is not stated, so ask.

items.en: Mouth-watering chicken in chilli oil
items.note: Poached chicken is clean; the sauce is not. Kou shui ji dressing is soy sauce, black vinegar and chilli oil, and Chinese black vinegar is frequently brewed from WHEAT or barley — two gluten routes in one dressing.

items.ja: とろけるポテトサラダ
items.en: Meltingly soft potato salad
items.note: Potato carries no wheat, but Japanese potato salad is bound with mayonnaise, which is egg — no for a vegan. Ask about the seasoning for gluten.

items.ja: パクチー肉味噌もやし
items.en: Bean sprouts with coriander and minced-pork miso
items.note: Pork, and 肉味噌 is built on miso and soy sauce — miso is itself frequently 麦味噌, barley.

items.en: Fried chicken
items.note: Karaage is dredged in flour or starch and marinated in soy sauce. Nothing here is labelled gluten-free, so this is the default answer.

items.en: Yurinchi — fried chicken with Kujo spring onion
items.note: Battered and fried, then dressed in a soy-and-vinegar sauce. Wheat on both sides.

items.en: Edamame with sansho pepper
items.note: The best prospect on this board for both diets: soybeans in the pod with pepper and salt. Plant-only, and nothing in the classic preparation needs wheat — but the seasoning is not stated and this is a kitchen full of soy sauce, so ask.

items.en: Char siu with fried egg
items.note: Char siu is braised or roasted in soy sauce; the egg rules out vegan.

items.en: Pan-fried gyoza, four pieces
items.note: Gyoza wrappers are wheat — that is what a gyoza is. Pan-fried gyoza is also normally finished with a wheat-starch slurry for the lacy crust, and the dipping sauce is soy and vinegar.

items.en: Boiled gyoza, four pieces
items.note: Gyoza wrappers are wheat — that is what a gyoza is. Boiled rather than fried, but the wrapper is unchanged and the water is shared.

items.en: Coriander boiled gyoza, four pieces
items.note: Gyoza wrappers are wheat — that is what a gyoza is.

items.en: Shiso boiled gyoza, four pieces
items.note: Gyoza wrappers are wheat — that is what a gyoza is.

items.en: Ban mian — sauced noodles without broth
items.note: Chinese wheat noodles in a soy-based sauce. Egg topping ¥50.

items.en: Chuka soba
items.note: Despite the そば in the name this is RAMEN — wheat noodles, not buckwheat — in a soy-seasoned broth. A naming trap worth knowing: 中華そば never means soba.

items.en: Chuka soba with a seasoned egg
items.note: Wheat noodles, and 味玉 is an egg marinated in soy.

items.ja: チャーシュー味玉中華そば
items.en: Chuka soba with char siu and a seasoned egg
items.note: Wheat noodles, soy-braised pork, soy-marinated egg.

items.en: Fried rice
items.note: Rice rather than noodles, which makes it the only substantial dish here worth asking about — but Chinese fried rice is nearly always finished with soy sauce, and it contains egg, so it is not vegan either way.

items.en: Double-egg fried rice
items.note: As the plain fried rice, with more egg.

items.en: Prawn and egg fried rice
items.note: As above, with prawn.

tokyo_tori_koji.price_note: Prices tax-included as printed by the shop, on a listing marked 公式 — published by the restaurant itself. PARTIAL, and here is exactly what is missing: the listing advertises 料理(4) à la carte items alongside these three courses, but those four are loaded by script and are not in the page a fetch receives, so they are not recorded rather than guessed at. The three courses below are complete and are the shop's own text. No allergen statement anywhere. ⚠ Two things a coeliac should know before booking: the courses are omakase — 「何が出てくるかは、その日のお楽しみ」 — so the skewers change daily and cannot be checked in advance, and there is a compulsory お通し at ¥700 whose contents are not published. There is no service charge. Closed Mondays; 西浅草, near Asakusa station on the Tsukuba Express.

items.en: The Tori Koji course, 8 items — starters, five yakitori skewers, the shop's popular finishing rice dish, and a dessert
items.note: The gluten question at any yakitori counter is タレ versus 塩: tare is a soy-sauce glaze and therefore wheat, while a salted skewer is just the bird over charcoal. This shop does not state which way it serves, and on an omakase set you do not choose — so the question to ask is whether the whole set can be done 塩で. A set course also removes the ability to skip anything: the 締め飯 (finishing rice) is undescribed and yakitori shops commonly finish on a soy-seasoned donburi or an oyako-don, and the dessert is unnamed. Chicken throughout rules out vegan.

items.en: Omakase seven-skewer set — the master picks the day's best, contents change daily, and one vegetable skewer is included
items.note: The gluten question at any yakitori counter is タレ versus 塩: tare is a soy-sauce glaze and therefore wheat, while a salted skewer is just the bird over charcoal. This shop does not state which way it serves, and on an omakase set you do not choose — so the question to ask is whether the whole set can be done 塩で. The shop states the contents change every day, so nothing about this set can be confirmed ahead of a visit. Worth noting for a vegetarian rather than a vegan: 野菜串を1本加え — one vegetable skewer is built into the set, but it is grilled over the same charcoal and basted from the same pot as the chicken.

items.en: Five-skewer set of the house favourites — the shop recommends it for a first visit
items.note: The gluten question at any yakitori counter is タレ versus 塩: tare is a soy-sauce glaze and therefore wheat, while a salted skewer is just the bird over charcoal. This shop does not state which way it serves, and on an omakase set you do not choose — so the question to ask is whether the whole set can be done 塩で. Described by the shop as the standard skewers rather than a daily-changing selection, which makes this the easier of the two sets to ask about in advance.

items.en: Compulsory seated charge
items.note: Not optional and not described. Worth flagging on both axes because an otoshi is served before anyone asks you anything — it is typically a small simmered or dressed dish, and at a Japanese counter that usually means dashi and soy sauce. The shop confirms 「お通し700円サービス料なし」: the ¥700 is charged but no service charge is added on top.

tokyo_hanwarai.price_note: No published menu: the Tabelog menu page returns 404, and the record's stored website — a shibuya-scramble-square.com shop page — is a DUMMY TEMPLATE serving placeholder text (ショップ名, この文章はダミーです) and 2019 lorem entries, so that URL is dead weight and should be replaced. The shop is real and trading on the 12th floor of Shibuya Scramble Square. Everything below comes from visitor accounts on the Tabelog listing — dishes ordered and prices paid — hence provisional. Useful context a visitor supplies: this is the sister shop of 玉笑 in Jingūmae, a soba house with a serious reputation, and 半笑 is where 玉笑 sends people when it is closed. Portions are on the small side by several accounts, and おかわり蕎麦 (a second board) can be ordered. Seating faces the wall.

items.en: The Scramble Square course — sesame tofu topped with yuba, a two-item plate of duck and itawasa, tamagoyaki in a dashi sauce with grated daikon, and a board of soba to finish
items.note: THE BUCKWHEAT-TO-WHEAT RATIO IS NOT PUBLISHED, which at a soba house is the only number that matters — Japanese soba is normally 二八, 80% buckwheat to 20% WHEAT. Even a 十割 kitchen dusts its boards with 打ち粉, usually wheat flour, and boils every order in shared water. The tsuyu is soy-based; a visitor describes it as やや甘め (on the sweet side) and another wished it were more strongly 醤油-forward. Soba tsuyu is also built on bonito dashi, so it is a vegan fact as much as a gluten one. As a set it is out on every course: the 板わさ is kamaboko, a fish cake commonly bound with wheat starch; the 玉子焼き arrives under a 出汁餡, a dashi sauce normally thickened and seasoned with soy; and the duck rules out vegan before any of that. A visitor records swapping the closing soba for the 野菜天せいろ, which replaces one wheat problem with a larger one.

items.ja: 湯葉をのせた胡麻豆腐
items.en: Sesame tofu topped with yuba
items.note: The one thing on this menu genuinely worth asking about, and it is buried inside a course. 胡麻豆腐 is not tofu at all — it is ground sesame set with KUDZU or arrowroot starch, so there is no soy and no wheat in the classic build, and 湯葉 is simply the skin off soy milk. Both are plant-only. What is not stated is the sauce: goma-dofu is usually served with a wasabi-soy or a dashi-based one, and a visitor mentions wasabi. Recorded without a price because it comes as part of the ¥1,980 course and no separate price is published.

items.en: Tamagoyaki under a dashi sauce with grated daikon
items.note: Praised by two visitors as the best thing on the course. Egg rules out vegan; the 出汁餡 is a soy-seasoned dashi sauce, normally thickened, and dashi is bonito. Part of the ¥1,980 course, so no separate price is published.

items.en: Soba with tempura and grated daikon — described by a visitor as an off-menu speciality at the sister shop 玉笑
items.note: Tempura batter is wheat flour, so this one is settled regardless of the noodle. THE BUCKWHEAT-TO-WHEAT RATIO IS NOT PUBLISHED, which at a soba house is the only number that matters — Japanese soba is normally 二八, 80% buckwheat to 20% WHEAT. The tsuyu is soy-based; a visitor describes it as やや甘め (on the sweet side) and another wished it were more strongly 醤油-forward. Soba tsuyu is also built on bonito dashi, so it is a vegan fact as much as a gluten one.

items.en: Seiro soba with vegetable tempura — aubergine, pumpkin, maitake, sweet potato and courgette
items.note: Available as a substitution for the closing soba on the 渋スクコース; a visitor records the swap but not a supplement price, so none is given. The vegetables would suit a vegan and the WHEAT BATTER does not suit anyone avoiding gluten — a good example of a dish that solves one diet and not the other. Even a 十割 kitchen dusts its boards with 打ち粉, usually wheat flour, and boils every order in shared water.

items.en: Seiro — chilled soba with dipping broth
items.note: The plain board. Visitors describe it as 田舎蕎麦風 with a strong buckwheat aroma, but none records a standalone price, so none is given here. THE BUCKWHEAT-TO-WHEAT RATIO IS NOT PUBLISHED, which at a soba house is the only number that matters — Japanese soba is normally 二八, 80% buckwheat to 20% WHEAT. The tsuyu is soy-based; a visitor describes it as やや甘め (on the sweet side) and another wished it were more strongly 醤油-forward. Soba tsuyu is also built on bonito dashi, so it is a vegan fact as much as a gluten one.

items.en: Sobayu — the water the soba was boiled in, served to finish
items.note: Every visitor account ends on it. Worth naming explicitly because it looks like a harmless cup of hot water and is not: sobayu IS the shared boiling water, carrying whatever came off every noodle cooked in it that service, including the 打ち粉 dusted on the boards. It is normally drunk mixed with the leftover soy-based tsuyu.

tokyo_oyasai_kozara_ryori_no_w.price_note: ⚠ TWO WARNINGS BEFORE THE PRICES. First, this menu carries an update date of 2017/09/28 — it is nearly nine years old, so treat every price as historical rather than current; the dishes are the shop's own text but the numbers will have moved. Second, THE SHOP'S OWN DOMAIN IS DEAD: vegan-kiboko.com no longer serves a site, returning a hosting error page reading ドメイン・ウェブの設定ができていません with the account described as non-existent, expired or deleted, and its TLS certificate belongs to the hosting provider (*.hpms1.jp) rather than the restaurant. Worth feeding to the dead-domain checker. The shop itself is trading — Tabelog carries the listing as 公式, closed Mondays, Tuesdays and Sundays. ⚠ HOW THE TWO DIETS SPLIT HERE: everything on this menu is vegan and a great deal of it is wheat. This is a vegetable wine bar built on gyoza wrappers, pasta and — most sharply — 車麩, which is pure wheat gluten and entirely plant-based. A vegan will eat very well; a coeliac vegan needs to read item by item, and the steamed vegetables are the safest thing on the page.

items.en: Coriander gyoza, four pieces — the shop says even people who dislike coriander finish them, and recommends white wine
items.note: Vegan on the shop's own blanket statement: 「動物性食材、卵、乳製品を使用せず」 and 「全てベジタリアン、ヴィーガン、ハラール、対応料理です」 — no animal ingredients, no egg, no dairy, across the whole board. Gyoza wrappers are wheat. A vegan gyoza is still a wheat gyoza.

items.ja: かぼちゃのスパニッシュオムレツ(1ピース）
items.en: Pumpkin Spanish omelette, one piece — the shop notes a French chef praised it and that it is fluffy despite using no egg
items.note: Vegan on the shop's own blanket statement: 「動物性食材、卵、乳製品を使用せず」 and 「全てベジタリアン、ヴィーガン、ハラール、対応料理です」 — no animal ingredients, no egg, no dairy, across the whole board. Genuinely interesting for a coeliac to ask about: an egg-free omelette has to be bound with something, and the two usual answers are chickpea flour, which is gluten-free, or wheat flour, which is not. The shop does not say which.

items.ja: 旬野菜のバーニャカウダ
items.en: Seasonal vegetable bagna cauda — the shop makes the point that it reaches this depth of flavour without anchovy
items.note: Vegan on the shop's own blanket statement: 「動物性食材、卵、乳製品を使用せず」 and 「全てベジタリアン、ヴィーガン、ハラール、対応料理です」 — no animal ingredients, no egg, no dairy, across the whole board. Bagna cauda is classically anchovy and garlic, so a vegan version is a real substitution rather than an omission. The dip itself is unlikely to carry wheat; bagna cauda is usually served with bread alongside the vegetables, which would.

items.en: Chili con carne — made with naturally cultivated beans instead of minced meat
items.note: Vegan on the shop's own blanket statement: 「動物性食材、卵、乳製品を使用せず」 and 「全てベジタリアン、ヴィーガン、ハラール、対応料理です」 — no animal ingredients, no egg, no dairy, across the whole board. Beans, tomato and spice have no structural wheat, which makes this one of the better prospects here. Nothing is declared, and chilli seasoning blends sometimes carry flour.

items.ja: 本日の全粒粉入りスパッゲッティ
items.en: Today's wholemeal spaghetti — the sauce is decided by what vegetables came in that day
items.note: Vegan on the shop's own blanket statement: 「動物性食材、卵、乳製品を使用せず」 and 「全てベジタリアン、ヴィーガン、ハラール、対応料理です」 — no animal ingredients, no egg, no dairy, across the whole board. Settled by the name: 全粒粉 is WHOLEMEAL WHEAT FLOUR. Wholemeal reads healthy and is no less wheat for it.

items.ja: 蒸しキムチギョーザ（大二個）
items.en: Steamed kimchi gyoza, two large — filled with kimchi the shop makes itself
items.note: Vegan on the shop's own blanket statement: 「動物性食材、卵、乳製品を使用せず」 and 「全てベジタリアン、ヴィーガン、ハラール、対応料理です」 — no animal ingredients, no egg, no dairy, across the whole board. Wheat wrappers. Worth noting the kimchi is house-made, which is what allows it to be vegan at all — commercial kimchi usually contains salted seafood.

items.en: KiboKo's karaage — the shop presents it as its answer to the long vegetarian problem of getting the texture right, and says it does not sit heavy
items.note: Vegan on the shop's own blanket statement: 「動物性食材、卵、乳製品を使用せず」 and 「全てベジタリアン、ヴィーガン、ハラール、対応料理です」 — no animal ingredients, no egg, no dairy, across the whole board. The coating is the whole question and is not stated. Karaage dredge is sometimes 片栗粉 (potato starch), which would be fine, and sometimes wheat flour, which would not — and the marinade is normally soy sauce. Ask about both.

No allergen statement anywhere, so every note below is inference from the dish. ⚠ READ THIS FIRST, BECAUSE IT DECIDES ALMOST EVERYTHING HERE: at an Indian restaurant the curry is usually the safe half and THE BREAD IS THE PROBLEM. These curries are built on onion, tomato and ground spice rather than the flour roux a Japanese カレー uses, so a curry ordered with RICE is a genuinely different proposition from the same curry with ナン — and naan is wheat bread, full stop. The shop lists four rice options (カオ, ライス, タイのもち米, ガーリックライス) against six breads, so the swap is easy to ask for. On the vegan axis the split runs the other way: there is a real vegetable and pulse curry list here, but Indian kitchens use ghee, cream and yoghurt freely and Thai kitchens use fish sauce and shrimp paste, so every plant dish still needs one question. tokyo_sushi_planet_suidobashi_.price_note: Read from the shop own official site. PARTIAL and here is what is missing: the site publishes ONE course in full and states that nigiri start at 1貫75円より (from 75 yen per piece), but it does not publish an itemised a la carte board with prices, so only the course is recorded. A photo caption names other items without prices; those are not recorded rather than priced by guess. No allergen statement. THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM HERE: this is a 江戸前寿司・天ぷら shop, so tempura is not a side dish but half the concept, and the same kitchen fries and forms sushi. Sushi rice and raw fish carry no wheat, but sushi is EATEN WITH SOY SAUCE and ordinary shoyu is wheat by default; whether tamari is available is not stated. A coeliac would need to ask about both the soy and the fryer. Advance reservation only for the course, which includes two hours of free drinks.

items.en: The Planet Full-Enjoyment course — six-item appetiser platter, three tempura, six nigiri, chawanmushi, prosciutto potato fries, a wagyu and caviar hand roll and miso soup; includes two hours of free drinks, advance reservation only
items.note: Not survivable as a set, and for more reasons than the obvious one. The 天ぷら3種 is wheat batter; the 茶碗蒸し is egg custard set with a dashi that is normally soy-seasoned; the 味噌汁 carries both a bonito dashi and a miso that is frequently 麦味噌, BARLEY, which no Japanese allergen label will flag; and the free-drink package is beer-led, and beer is barley too. Fish, egg and wagyu rule out vegan several times over.

items.en: Six-item appetiser platter, part of the course
items.note: Contents are not published anywhere on the site. At a Japanese counter an appetiser platter normally means simmered and dressed dishes, which means dashi and soy sauce.

items.ja: 天ぷら３種盛り（海老・キス・野菜）
items.en: Three tempura — prawn, whiting and vegetable, part of the course
items.note: Tempura batter is wheat flour, and the tentsuyu it is dipped in is a soy-and-dashi broth. The 野菜 piece would suit a vegan were it not battered and fried in shared oil.

items.ja: 握り6貫盛り（まぐろ・はまち・たい・ボイル海老・トロたく・玉子）
items.en: Six nigiri — tuna, yellowtail, sea bream, boiled prawn, toro-taku and egg, part of the course
items.note: The rice and the raw fish are clean; what is not is what goes on them. Sushi is eaten with soy sauce, nigiri are brushed with a soy nikiri at an Edomae counter, and the 玉子 is a sweet omelette normally made with mirin and soy and sometimes flour. トロたく is a roll, so it also carries nori and takuan. Ask whether tamari is available.

items.en: Chawanmushi with aosa seaweed, part of the course
items.note: Savoury egg custard set with dashi — bonito, and the seasoning is normally 白だし or だし醤油, both soy. Egg rules out vegan.

items.en: Prosciutto potato fries, part of the course
items.note: Potato and cured pork. Chips are often flour-dusted, and this kitchen fries tempura in the same oil.

items.en: Wagyu and caviar hand roll, part of the course
items.note: A nori hand roll — the wrapper is seaweed, not wheat. The seasoning on the wagyu is the open question and is normally soy-based.

items.en: Aosa seaweed miso soup, part of the course
items.note: Two things a miso soup hides: the dashi is normally bonito, which ends the vegan question, and the miso itself is frequently 麦味噌 — BARLEY — which is not on Japan statutory allergen list and so is never labelled.

items.en: Nigiri, a la carte — the shop states prices start from 75 yen per piece
items.note: The starting price is the shop own; individual neta and their prices are not published, so no items are listed. The standing caveat applies to all of them: sushi is eaten with soy sauce, and an Edomae counter brushes nikiri onto the fish before it reaches you, so the wheat arrives without being ordered. Ask about tamari.

tokyo_dixans_suidobashi_dizon.price_note: The Tabelog menu page returns 404; this comes from the café's own page and the Retty board it links to. PARTIAL, and the gap is specific: the DRINKS carry prices and the CAKES DO NOT — Retty lists five patisserie items by name with no price against any of them, so they are recorded without prices rather than given invented ones. No allergen, gluten or vegan statement anywhere. ⚠ THIS IS A DESSERT CAFÉ, WHICH MEANS THE TWO DIETS FARE VERY DIFFERENTLY: the drinks list is long and much of it is fine for both, while every cake is patisserie and dairy. A vegan has essentially nothing to eat here and plenty to drink — and the drinks are where to ask, since a milk alternative would decide most of the list. The shop notes that beyond coffee it also serves tea and herbal tea, and the black tea is CLIPPER, with a choice of leaf.

tokyo_conrow_shibuya_dogenzaka.price_note: Prices tax-included as printed on the shop's Tabelog menu; the restaurant's own site lists the same dishes by name but publishes no prices, so the numbers come from Tabelog. No allergen statement on either. The shop notes the board differs slightly between its Shibuya and Ebisu branches and that seasonal specials run beyond what is listed. ⚠ HOW THIS CUISINE SPLITS THE TWO DIETS, because it is not the usual way round: Thai food is largely RICE-BASED — rice noodles, jasmine rice, sticky rice, rice-paper rolls — so a coeliac has far more to work with here than at most restaurants in this dataset, and the wheat is concentrated in the deep-fried section and the OYSTER SAUCE that seasons the stir-fries. A vegan has the harder time: fish sauce and shrimp paste are foundational, so even the vegetable dishes need a question. The 空芯菜の辛味噌炒め is the closest thing to a plant main and it is still made with 辛味噌 and almost certainly fish sauce. Note also that every item comes with a salad (※全てにサラダが付きます), whose dressing is undeclared.

items.en: Thai prawn crackers
items.note: No price listed on the board. Prawn crackers are usually tapioca starch and prawn, which makes them wheat-free in the classic form — but the recipe is not stated. Prawn rules out vegan.

tokyo_tsurutontan_udon_noodle_.price_note: Prices tax-included as printed on the shop's Tabelog menu; the chain's own menu page lists seasonal dishes by name but publishes no prices, so the numbers come from Tabelog. No allergen statement on either. Shibuya Scramble Square 13F, open daily 11:00–23:00. ⚠ SAY THE OBVIOUS THING PLAINLY: this is an udon house, udon is wheat, and roughly half this menu is therefore closed to a coeliac before any question is asked. It is recorded in full anyway, because the useful information is WHERE THE EXCEPTIONS ARE — and they are not where you would expect. The noodle sections are uniformly out. The sushi and 逸品 sections are raw fish and rice, limited only by the soy sauce. And the dessert list is the one place a coeliac genuinely has choices: くずきり is kudzu starch and わらびもち is bracken starch, both traditionally wheat-free and both plant-only. A vegan, by contrast, has almost nothing here — the dashi alone rules out the entire noodle menu.

PARTIAL: the 飯もん (rice) section and the drinks list run past the point captured here and are not recorded rather than guessed at; everything above them is complete. No allergen statement. ⚠ THIS SHOP IS THREE WHEAT PROBLEMS STACKED, and it is worth naming them separately because they are not the same problem. (1) KUSHIKATSU is panko-crumbed and deep-fried — the coating is the dish, so a vegetable skewer is no safer than a beef one. (2) The DIPPING SAUCE is communal by tradition and Worcester-based, so it is soy and usually wheat. (3) ODEN simmers everything together in one soy-and-dashi pot. What is genuinely useful here is the 冷たいもん (cold dishes) section, which is the only part of the menu that avoids all three — and even there the shop names its own miso as 麦味噌, BARLEY, which is not on Japan's statutory allergen list and will never appear on a label. Every kushikatsu is a flat ¥264 or below on the shop's "cheap and good" framing, and the ¥55 pork belly is limited to five per person.

tokyo_sobashonin_komagata_soba.price_note: No published menu: the Tabelog menu page returns 404 and the shop has no site of its own — the record's stored website is the Tabelog listing itself. Everything below comes from visitor accounts on that listing, so it is provisional, and NO PRICES ARE RECORDED because no visitor states one; Tabelog gives only a ¥2,000–2,999 band for the shop as a whole. ⚠ WHAT MAKES THIS SHOP UNUSUAL, AND WHY IT IS UNRESOLVED: this is a 変わり蕎麦 house — its draw is soba flavoured and coloured by kneading other ingredients into the dough, served as a 三色 or 五色 flight of three or five different noodles on one tray. Visitors name けしきり (poppy seed), れもんきり (lemon), しそきり (shiso), 茶きり (tea), ゆずきり (yuzu), さくらきり (cherry, April only), plus plain せいろ and coarse 田舎. Every one of those is a different dough, and the shop states the composition of none of them. So a coeliac faces not one unanswered ratio question here but five or six, on a tray where the varieties are boiled together. The daily lineup rotates. Asakusa, a five-to-six-minute walk from the Ginza line station; tables downstairs, tatami rooms upstairs.

items.en: Three-colour soba — a choice of three noodles from five, on one tray
items.note: A visitor records choosing けしきり, れもんきり and しそきり from five available. THE BUCKWHEAT-TO-WHEAT RATIO IS NOT PUBLISHED for any variety here, and at a soba house that is the only number that decides anything — Japanese soba is normally 二八, 80% buckwheat to 20% WHEAT. Even a 十割 kitchen dusts its boards with 打ち粉, usually wheat flour, and boils every order in shared water. The tsuyu is soy-based and built on bonito dashi, so it is a second wheat route and rules out vegan independently of the noodle.

Tabelog carries an explicit warning on this listing — 「税込金額か不明の価格です。正確な価格は店舗へ直接ご確認ください」, meaning it does not know whether these figures are tax-inclusive and says to confirm with the shop. Every other record in this dataset states tax-included prices, so this one is the exception and the numbers below could be up to 10% higher at the till. ⚠ ON THE FOOD: 洋食 is Japan's domesticated Western cooking, and it is one of the most consistently wheat-heavy categories there is — the fried section is flour, egg and panko throughout, the stews are built on a browned roux, and the curry is a roux curry. There is no gluten-free order on this menu and the salads are the only things that come close. A vegan has less than that: even the plain 生野菜 salad is the only item with no declared animal ingredient, and its dressing is unstated. Recorded in full so the answer is visible rather than absent. 浅草1-15-1; closed Sundays; lunch 11:30–14:00 and dinner 17:00–20:00. But read the word carefully: ベジタリアン means VEGETARIAN, not vegan. The gelato and the soy pudding both carry the mark, and one of those is far more likely to suit a vegan than the other. The label also says nothing about gluten, and this is a DUMPLING shop — the house speciality is water gyoza, and every wrapper, bun and roll on the board is wheat. The clean split here is that the labelled vegetable dishes are also the only dishes with any gluten prospect, because they are the ones with no wrapper. No allergen statement beyond the vegetarian marks. The signature 肉汁水餃子 is ¥1,089 for four, ¥1,420 for six and ¥2,380 for ten, made with 100% Kagoshima black pork.

tokyo_shinjuku_kominka_juttoku.price_note: No menu published anywhere readable. The shop's own site carries its concept, hours and seating but no dishes and no prices; the Tabelog menu page returns 404. The five dishes below are ones visitors name having eaten, with NO PRICES because no visitor states one — Tabelog gives only a ¥5,000–5,999 band for the shop. ⚠ WHAT THIS KIND OF PLACE MEANS FOR BOTH DIETS: it bills itself as 全国郷土の味巡り, a tour of regional Japanese cooking, in a converted old house — and regional washoku is the category where DASHI and SOY SAUCE are in nearly everything, including dishes that look plain. Bonito dashi is a vegan fact and a gluten fact at once, since 白だし, めんつゆ and だし醤油 are all soy-based. A sake izakaya is also a barley room: beer is barley and 麦焼酎 is barley, neither flagged by Japanese allergen labelling. One thing a visitor establishes that is genuinely useful: at lunch, rice and miso soup come with free refills. Open from 16:00 Tuesday to Friday; 50 seats with tatami and counter. Note for the record: a visitor mentions 十徳新宿本店 was closed for renovation to the end of August and trading from an annexe — that is the separate HONTEN, not this shop, and is not recorded as a closure here.

tokyo_waiwaitei.price_note: ⚠ TWO PRICE WARNINGS, BOTH FROM TABELOG ITSELF. First, this menu carries an update date of 2019/06/24 — it is about seven years old, so treat every figure as historical. Second, Tabelog states 「税込金額か不明の価格です。正確な価格は店舗へ直接ご確認ください」: it does not know whether these prices include tax. Most records in this dataset state tax-inclusive prices; this is the second one that cannot. ⚠ THE ONE THING ON THIS MENU WORTH A COELIAC'S ATTENTION, and it needs stating carefully because it is not confirmed: the pizza section contains a line reading 野菜ライス生地PIZZA — a vegetable RICE-DOUGH pizza. A rice-flour base at an Italian restaurant would be a genuine find. But the listing is ambiguous about whether that line is a dish or a heading introducing a rice-dough crust option for the pizzas beneath it, it carries no price, and NO GLUTEN-FREE CLAIM IS MADE ANYWHERE. Even if the base is rice, it would be rolled on the same bench and baked in the same oven as wheat dough. Worth a phone call; not worth an assumption. A second alternative crust, じゃことたまご生地PIZZA (whitebait and egg dough, ¥800), sits nearby and is equally undescribed. Otherwise this is a pasta-and-pizza house and the answer is uniform. Two accommodation notes the shop does volunteer: 「辛さ調整いたします」 (heat adjusted to taste) and 「ご要望ございましたらその他お作りいたします」 (they will make other things on request) — which is the sort of kitchen where asking is worth doing. tokyo_hokkaido_meibutsu_ramen_.price_note: Prices tax-included as printed by the shop. No allergen statement. ⚠ Two straightforward facts and one worth pausing on. The straightforward ones: this is a ramen shop, ramen noodles are WHEAT, and every broth here is a 甘エビ (sweet shrimp) stock, so nothing on the board suits a vegan and nothing suits a coeliac. The one worth pausing on is the NOODLE CHOICE — the shop invites you to pick 太麺 or 細麺, thick or thin. That is the situation where someone might hope a shop offers a rice or buckwheat alternative, and here as at other shops in this dataset the choice is between two kinds of wheat. Recorded in full so the answer is visible rather than absent. No reservations; 西新宿7-8-2, three minutes from Shinjuku-nishiguchi.

tokyo_chuka_soba_katsumoto.price_note: Read from the shop's own English page; prices stated tax-inclusive by the shop. No allergen statement. ⚠ THE NAMING TRAP IS THE WHOLE STORY HERE, and it is worth stating because this dataset will keep meeting it: 中華そば means RAMEN. The そば is a historical usage meaning "noodle", not buckwheat — so a coeliac scanning for そば and hoping for buckwheat finds wheat. The shop is explicit that its 中細麺 are made for it alone by 浅草開化楼, a specialist noodle maker, which is a mark of quality and not of composition. Every bowl here is wheat. The rice dishes are the only part of the board that is not, and they are recorded with their own caveats. Frozen three-portion sets are sold to take away and via Amazon.

items.en: Extra noodles

items.en: Roasted seaweed topping
items.note: Plain toasted seaweed — sheet nori and nothing else, which makes it one of only two toppings here with no route to either diet. Note this holds only for 焼海苔; 味付海苔 would be seasoned with soy.

items.en: Seasoned boiled egg
items.note: Marinated in a soy tare. Egg.

items.en: Scallions
items.note: Sliced spring onion — the other clean topping on the board.

items.en: Seasoned bamboo shoots
items.note: Bamboo shoot is a plant and vegan, but this one is 味付 — seasoned, which at a ramen shop means soy sauce. A neat illustration of the two axes disagreeing on a single ¥150 topping.

items.en: Three slices of pork belly chashu
items.note: Soy-braised pork.

items.en: Rice
items.note: Plain steamed rice — the one thing in this shop with no route to either diet. Large ¥250.

items.en: Rice with raw egg and dried salted kelp
items.note: Raw egg rules out vegan, and TKG is dressed with soy sauce as a matter of course. 塩昆布 is also commonly seasoned with soy in manufacture — two routes in a dish that looks like rice and an egg.

items.en: Pork belly claypot rice
items.note: Claypot rice is cooked in a seasoned stock, and pork belly at a ramen shop is soy-braised.

items.en: Frozen chuka soba to take away, three portions
items.note: The same wheat noodles and soy-based soup, frozen. Two portions ¥2,000, one ¥1,100. Also sold via Amazon.

tokyo_vegego_miyashita_park.price_note: ⚠⚠ READ THE NAME CAREFULLY: VEGEGO IS NOT A VEGAN RESTAURANT. This is the correction this record exists to make. The name and the brand's 野菜 framing read as plant-based, and it is not — the chain's own site presents 究極のスンドゥブ made with BEEF AND SEAFOOD and 自家製サムゲタン, a chicken soup, among its four signature dishes, and the Tokyo branch is filed on Tabelog as 韓国料理. It is a vegetable-forward Korean restaurant, which is a different thing entirely, and anyone arriving on the strength of the name would be misled. NO PRICES ARE RECORDED, and here is exactly why: the branch page carries no menu, the Tabelog menu page returns 404, and the chain publishes its mall-format board only as a PDF whose text layer is EMPTY — it is an image, so nothing in it can be read. The dish names below come from the chain's own site; the board is the mall format rather than this branch specifically, so it may vary. No allergen, gluten or vegan statement appears anywhere on any page read. RAYARD MIYASHITA PARK South 3F, 11:00–21:00.

items.en: Stone-grilled bibimbap
items.section: グランドメニュー Grand menu
items.note: Rice and vegetables in a hot stone bowl, which is why people assume bibimbap is safe — but it is dressed with gochujang, and Korean chilli paste is traditionally made with wheat flour or barley malt, a gluten route most people never associate with Korean food. Normally topped with a fried egg, and often minced beef.

items.en: The house special bibimbap — the chain describes it as vegetable-heavy
items.section: グランドメニュー Grand menu
items.note: Named by the chain as a signature. Same gochujang question as the stone-bowl version; the vegetable emphasis narrows the vegan question without answering it, since bibimbap conventionally carries egg and beef.

items.ja: プレミアムチーズダッカルビ
items.en: Premium cheese dakgalbi
items.section: グランドメニュー Grand menu
items.note: Dakgalbi is chicken marinated in gochujang, and the cheese is dairy — out on both axes.

items.ja: 塩麹漬厚切りサムギョプサル
items.en: Thick-cut samgyeopsal marinated in salt koji
items.section: グランドメニュー Grand menu
items.note: Worth one question rather than a flat no: 塩麹 is rice koji and salt, which unlike a soy marinade has no wheat in its classic form — so the pork itself may be clean. Samgyeopsal is conventionally eaten with ssamjang, a soybean-and-gochujang paste, which is not. Ask whether it can come without.

items.en: Ultimate Pyongyang naengmyeon
items.section: グランドメニュー Grand menu
items.note: The most interesting item here for a coeliac and it is genuinely open. Pyongyang-style naengmyeon is classically BUCKWHEAT with a little potato starch — not wheat, unlike Japanese 冷やし中華 — and a shop naming the Pyongyang style specifically is claiming that tradition. Nothing states the ratio, and Korean buckwheat noodles are commonly cut with wheat or sweet potato starch. The broth is a chilled beef or dongchimi stock. Worth asking the ratio.

items.en: Ultimate sundubu — the chain states it is made with beef and seafood
items.section: グランドメニュー Grand menu
items.note: The dish that most clearly disproves the name: the chain itself describes this soft-tofu stew as containing BEEF AND SEAFOOD. The broth is gochujang- and gochugaru-based.

items.en: House-made samgyetang — ginseng chicken soup with vegetables
items.section: グランドメニュー Grand menu
items.note: Chicken, so never vegan. But the best coeliac prospect on this board and worth naming as such: samgyetang is a whole chicken stuffed with glutinous RICE, ginseng and jujube, simmered in plain water and salted at the table — no soy sauce and no gochujang in the classic build, which is what rules out nearly everything else here. Undeclared, so still ask.

items.ja: 本格仕込みの水キムチ
items.en: Properly made water kimchi
items.section: グランドメニュー Grand menu
items.note: A better prospect than ordinary kimchi on both axes, which is worth knowing: 水キムチ is fermented in a light brine rather than the chilli-and-seafood paste used for 白菜キムチ, so it is more often free of both the salted seafood and the wheat-flour porridge that make regular kimchi a double question. Neither is declared here, so it is still a question — just a more hopeful one.

items.en: Croffle
items.note: A croffle is croissant dough pressed in a waffle iron — wheat pastry, and croissant dough is made with butter.

tokyo_uogashi_nihon_ichi_tachi.price_note: ⚠⚠ THE PRICES BELOW ARE ALMOST CERTAINLY WRONG NOW, and that matters more than usual here. This menu carries an update date of 2017/11/13 — nearly nine years old — and its cheapest band is 1貫75円 (¥81 with tax). A standing sushi bar in Shibuya at ¥81 a piece in 2026 is not credible, so treat every figure as a historical record of the shop's BAND STRUCTURE rather than as money. The structure itself is the useful part and is likely to have survived: neta are grouped into fixed price tiers, everything is served two pieces at a time, and the hand-rolls sit on their own flat prices. ⚠ ON GLUTEN, THE ANSWER IS SIMPLE AND IT IS NOT ABOUT THE FISH: raw fish and vinegared rice contain no wheat, so almost everything here is ask rather than no — what rules a piece out is the SOY SAUCE it is dipped in, and at a standing counter the bottle is communal. Four items are settled rather than askable because the wheat is cooked into them: the 玉子, the soy-simmered 煮あさり and あなご, the 納豆 with its sachet tare, and the かんぴょう. Nothing here is vegan except the cucumber roll, and even that depends on the soy. No allergen statement. No reservations; standing only.

items.en: Pickled vegetable hand roll

items.en: Cucumber hand roll

items.en: Fatty tuna and pickled radish hand roll

tokyo_jidoriya_tsukada_shibuya.price_note: Read from the restaurant's own site. No allergen statement, though the shop does publish one food-safety note: its raw chicken dishes (むね身たたき, ももたたき, ささみ昆布〆) use meat processed by 塩せき熟成ハム製法 to meet the standard for non-heat-treated meat products. That is a safety assurance about raw chicken, not an allergen declaration. ⚠ WHERE THE OPENING IS: this is a charcoal and hotpot house rather than a fried one, which makes it a better prospect than most izakaya in this dataset — but the wheat is concentrated in the DIPS AND DRESSINGS rather than the food, so almost everything turns on one question asked at the table. The 水炊き is the item worth travelling for: a Hakata-style chicken mizutaki is chicken simmered in water, with nothing else in the pot, and what would rule it out is only the ponzu it is dipped in. The 炭火焼 is the same shape of question — 塩 or タレ. Against that, the 春巻き and メンチカツ are settled wheat, and anything named 醤油 or ユッケ is settled too. There is a compulsory ¥550 お通し whose contents are not published. Nothing here suits a vegan: it is a jidori chicken specialist and even the two vegetable dishes are dressed with egg yolk or served alongside chicken. 道玄坂2-6-1 渋谷岩崎ビル 3F; 50 seats, entirely non-smoking.

items.en: Jidori mizutaki course — seasonal soup, four-item appetiser, three-variety sashimi, charcoal-grilled chicken, a small bowl, fried hand wing, a palate cleanser and the mizutaki hotpot
items.note: The hotpot at the centre of this course is the best thing here for a coeliac, but the course around it is not: it includes a 手羽先の唐揚げ (fried wing), which is flour-dredged, and the appetiser and small bowl are undescribed, which at a Japanese counter means dashi and soy. A set course also removes the ability to decline anything. Per person.

items.en: Charcoal-grilled jidori chicken
items.note: The second-best prospect on this menu and the question is a single word: 塩 or タレ. Chicken over charcoal with salt has no wheat route at all; a tare is a soy glaze and does. The shop does not say which it serves, so ask for 塩で.

items.ja: 希少部位の炭火焼 レバー
items.en: Charcoal-grilled liver, a rare cut
items.note: Grilled rather than crumbed; liver is usually served with a tare, so ask for salt.

items.en: Jidori mizutaki hotpot, one portion
items.note: ⚠ THE ITEM WORTH ASKING ABOUT PROPERLY. 水炊き means "cooked in water" and that is literally the method — Hakata-style mizutaki is chicken and water, simmered until the broth turns milky from the collagen, with no soy sauce, no miso and no dashi packet in the pot. On a menu where nearly everything carries a soy-based dressing, this is the one dish whose cooking method has no wheat route at all. What it is served WITH does: mizutaki is eaten with ponzu, which is citrus plus SOY SAUCE and normally bonito. Ask whether salt and citrus can come instead of the ponzu, and this becomes a real meal.

items.ja: 地鶏ときのこのしゃぶすき＜1人前＞
items.en: Jidori and mushroom shabu-sukiyaki, one portion
items.note: The sister dish to the mizutaki and the opposite answer: すき means sukiyaki, and sukiyaki is simmered in warishita — soy sauce, mirin and sugar. The wheat is in the broth here rather than the dip. Worth putting beside the 水炊き to see how much the cooking liquid decides.

items.ja: 地鶏刺身盛り合わせ（３種）
items.en: Three assorted jidori sashimi
items.note: Raw chicken carries no wheat. The shop states these use meat processed by 塩せき熟成ハム製法 to clear the standard for non-heat-treated meat — a safety note, not an allergen one. The dipping sauce is the gluten question and is normally soy.

items.ja: 地鶏ささみとアボカドのわさび醤油
items.romaji: jidori sasami to abokado no wasabi jōyu
items.en: Jidori tender and avocado in wasabi soy
items.note: Settled by its own name: 醤油 is soy sauce, and soy sauce is wheat by default.

items.ja: 地鶏の白レバー刺し（低温調理）
items.en: Jidori white liver sashimi, low-temperature cooked
items.note: Liver cooked sous-vide and served cold; the accompaniment is undeclared and is usually a soy-based dip or a sesame oil and salt.

items.ja: 地鶏のユッケ（低温調理）
items.en: Jidori yukke, low-temperature cooked
items.note: Yukke dressing is soy-based and normally carries gochujang, which is itself commonly made with wheat flour or barley malt. Contains raw egg yolk as standard.

items.ja: 地鶏と梅水晶の梅肉和え
items.romaji: jidori to umesuishō no bainiku ae
items.en: Jidori with shark cartilage in plum paste
items.note: Umebishio is salt-cured plum, which has no wheat in its traditional form — but 梅水晶 is a commercial preparation of shark cartilage and umeboshi that is normally seasoned with soy or mirin. Ask.

items.ja: 季節野菜の黄身酢和え
items.en: Seasonal vegetables in egg-yolk vinegar dressing
items.note: The only vegetable dish on the menu, and it is not vegan: 黄身酢 is an egg yolk and vinegar dressing. Kimizu is classically yolk, vinegar, sugar and salt with no wheat, but many versions add 白だし. Ask.

items.ja: 地鶏むね肉のよだれ鶏（低温調理）
items.en: Jidori breast, mouth-watering chicken style, low-temperature cooked
items.note: The chicken is poached and clean; the dressing is not. Kou shui ji is soy sauce, black vinegar and chilli oil, and Chinese black vinegar is frequently brewed from WHEAT or barley — two routes in the one sauce.

items.ja: 地鶏のチーズ明太春巻き＜1本＞
items.en: Jidori, cheese and mentaiko spring roll, one piece
items.note: Spring roll wrappers are wheat. Mentaiko is soy-cured and the cheese is dairy.

items.en: Jidori menchi katsu, one piece
items.note: Panko breadcrumbs are wheat bread, and menchi katsu filling is normally bound with breadcrumb as well.

items.en: Seasonal claypot rice — price listed as ASK
items.note: The shop prints ASK against this rather than a price, so none is given here. Contents change with the season and are not published. Claypot rice is normally cooked in a seasoned dashi stock, which would be both a wheat and an animal route, so both axes are genuinely open.

items.en: Compulsory cover dish, per person
items.note: Not optional and not described. Worth flagging on both axes because an otoshi arrives before anyone asks you anything — it is typically a small simmered or dressed dish, and at a Japanese counter that usually means dashi and soy sauce.

items.en: The house custard pudding
items.note: A custard pudding is egg, milk and caramel with no flour in the classic build — the better of the two desserts for a coeliac. Dairy and egg rule out vegan.

items.ja: さつまいものバスクチーズケーキ
items.en: Sweet potato Basque cheesecake
items.note: A Basque cheesecake is baked without a base, which is why it is worth asking about rather than assuming — but the batter normally contains a little flour or cornflour, and this one is not described. Dairy and egg.

items.en: Aokage shochu with ginger
items.note: ⚠ 青鹿毛 is a MUGI shochu — barley. Distillation removes most gluten protein and many coeliacs treat spirits as safe, but this dataset does not make that call for anyone, and barley is not on Japan's statutory allergen list so nothing will flag it.

items.en: Grilled lemon sour
items.note: The base shochu is not named. If it is 麦焼酎 that is barley; if 芋 or 米, it is not. Worth asking which.

items.ja: にっぽんフレッシュリレーサワー
items.en: Nippon fresh relay sour — rotating seasonal fruit
items.note: Base shochu unnamed; fruit rotates.

items.en: Forest-scented sudachi sour
items.note: Base shochu unnamed.

items.ja: イル・ポッジョ・スプマンテ
items.en: Il Poggio Spumante
items.note: Wine is grape, with no wheat route. Vegan is genuinely open: many wines are fined with isinglass, gelatin or egg white, and no Japanese menu says.

items.ja: アルガブランカ クラレーザ
items.en: Alga Branca Clareza
items.note: Japanese white wine; the fining question above applies. アルガーノ クラン ¥900.

items.ja: フレッシュレモネード
items.en: Fresh lemonade
items.note: Lemon, sugar and water — one of the few things here with no route to either diet.

items.ja: クラフトジンジャーソーダ
items.en: Craft ginger soda
items.note: Ginger syrup and soda water.

tokyo_asakusa_amairo.price_note: No published menu: the Tabelog menu page returns 404 and the shop has no site of its own — the record's stored website is the Tabelog listing. What follows comes from visitor accounts on that listing, so it is provisional and covers only what people happened to order. ⚠ THE HONEST ANSWER FOR BOTH DIETS IS NO, AND SAYING IT ONCE IS MORE USEFUL THAN HEDGING: this is a tempura and tendon specialist. Tempura is flour-battered and deep-fried, the tare is soy-based, and there is no dish here that avoids both. Even the vegetable pieces a vegan might hope for — the broccoli and sweet potato a visitor names — are battered in the same wheat and fried in the same oil, and the batter normally contains egg. Recorded so the answer is visible rather than absent. Two useful details from visitors: queues form at lunch, and the shop provides a separate plate to rest pieces on, which is thoughtful but does nothing about shared oil. Tabelog price band ¥4,000–4,999, which visitors' actual spends undercut considerably.

items.en: Tempura rice bowl — two prawns with white fish and vegetables
items.note: Tempura batter is WHEAT FLOUR, and the tare poured over a tendon is soy, mirin and sugar — so a tendon is wheat twice over, in the coating and in the sauce. A visitor records ¥1,300 and calls it the most reasonable option, noting the tare soaks well into the rice. tokyo_tofu_kawakaze.price_note: ⚠ THIS SHOP'S EXISTENCE IS NOT CONFIRMED AND THE RECORD IS HIDDEN IN THE APP. Tabelog has suspended the listing (掲載保留 — operating status unverifiable) and the shop's domain tofu-kawakaze.com no longer resolves. The menu below is recorded so it survives if the shop is confirmed trading; do not treat it as current. ⚠ WHY IT WOULD BE WORTH CONFIRMING: a tofu-and-yuba house is one of the few Japanese restaurant formats where a vegan has genuine choices, because the centre of the menu is soybean rather than fish or meat. But read it carefully rather than hopefully — this is an izakaya as well as a tofu specialist, most of the board is chicken, pork and fish, and the tofu dishes themselves are mostly dressed with dashi, soy or miso. 湯葉刺し and ざる豆腐 are the two that come closest to plant-only, and both are conventionally served with a soy dip. 浅草3-34-11; dinner only on weekdays, lunch at weekends, closed Mondays.

tokyo_swing_suidobashi_ten.price_note: Read from the shop's Tabelog menu; the record's stored website is an Instagram account, which is not a menu this dataset can cite. No allergen statement. ⚠ THE SHAPE OF THIS MENU FOR A COELIAC: it is a Western-style dining bar, so the wheat is in the obvious places — pasta, pizza, the roux dishes (curry, hayashi, gratin), the fried section and the baguette that comes with half the小皿. What is worth knowing is that a lot of dishes here are wheat only BECAUSE OF THE BREAD BESIDE THEM: the ajillos, the beef-tendon red wine stew and the curry all arrive バケット付, and asking for them without would change several answers. The other genuine prospect is the SAUSAGE SECTION — the shop names a German supplier and an IFFA certification, and German Wurst traditionally carries no cereal filler, unlike Japanese sausage. For a vegan the pickings are thin but real: pickles, olives, nuts, tomato salad and the vegetable sticks. 「生地はクリスピータイプです」 — the pizza base is a crisp one, and it is still wheat.

items.en: German plate
items.note: Worth asking about rather than assuming: the shop names its supplier as マイスター東金屋, states the sausages are made 添加物を極限まで排し (with additives kept to a minimum) and that they are IFFA-certified in Frankfurt. German Wurst is traditionally meat, fat and spice with no cereal filler, unlike Japanese sausage which is commonly bulked with wheat rusk — so a German-certified sausage is a genuinely better prospect than the category usually is. tokyo_yashima_maruyamacho_ten_.price_note: NO PRICES ARE RECORDED. The Tabelog menu page carries no items, and the shop's own page shows featured dishes without prices — so the five below are names only, and none carries an invented figure. Tabelog gives a ¥2,000–2,999 band for the shop as a whole. ⚠ THIS IS THE CLEAREST NOODLE STATEMENT IN THE DATASET, AND IT IS A NEGATIVE ONE. Most soba and udon shops leave a coeliac guessing at the flour; this one publishes it. THE SHOP STATES ITS OWN FLOUR: it blends 強力粉 and 中力粉 — strong and medium WHEAT flour — across four or five varieties, adjusted by the chef each year, with the dough aged three days and the noodles kneaded and cut by hand rather than by machine. That is an unusually precise description of a noodle, and every word of it is wheat. There is no ambiguity to chase here and no ratio to ask about — Sanuki udon is wheat by definition, and this shop is proud of exactly which wheats. Recorded so the answer is visible rather than absent. For a vegan the second problem is the broth: udon tsuyu is dashi and soy, so both axes close on the same bowl. 円山町10-13, Shibuya.

tokyo_nepalico_shibuya_nepalic.price_note: ⚠ ONE OF THE BEST RECORDS IN THIS DATASET FOR BOTH DIETS, AND FOR REASONS THE SHOP ITSELF SUPPLIES. It marks vegetarian dishes with a V and prints the legend ※V＝Veg Menu — read that as VEGETARIAN rather than vegan, since it says nothing about dairy or ghee. More unusually, it STATES THE FLOUR IN TWO DISHES, which almost no restaurant does: its ポコラ is bound with ひよこ豆の粉 (CHICKPEA flour) and its チョタモリ is built on 米粉の生地 (a RICE-FLOUR base). Both are naturally gluten-free flours, named by the kitchen rather than inferred. Against that, its チャパティ is explicitly 全粒粉 — wholemeal WHEAT — and the モモ are wheat-wrapped dumplings. The structural point is that Nepali food is rice-and-lentil based: the ダルバート sets are rice, dal, tarkari, achar, sag and papad, and the shop gives free refills of dal and rice with them. Curry heat is adjustable 0 to 3 ピロ, and the shop notes the vegetable and chicken curries are effectively heat-0. Selected for Tabelog's アジア・エスニック TOKYO 百名店 2026.

tokyo_jidori_kaisen_juwari_sob.price_note: Read from the restaurant's own site. PARTIAL: the site publishes its courses with prices and three headline dishes with prices, but not an itemised à la carte board, so only what it states is recorded. Note the headline prices are marked 税抜 — BEFORE TAX — which is unusual in this dataset and means roughly 10% more at the till; the course prices are marked 税込. ⚠ THIS IS THE FIRST SHOP IN THE DATASET TO CLAIM 十割 IN ITS OWN WORDS, so read the item note carefully rather than the shop name. THE SHOP CLAIMS 十割 WITH NO BINDER: 「日日の蕎麦は、石臼挽きのそば粉に香りの強い『玄粉』を合わせ、つなぎを使わない『十割』でご用意しております」 — stone-milled buckwheat blended with strongly aromatic 玄粉, made 十割 with NO つなぎ. つなぎ is the binder, and at a soba shop the binder is wheat flour, so this is the kitchen stating in its own words that there is no wheat IN the dough. That is a genuinely better starting point than almost any soba shop in this dataset. ⚠ IT IS NOT THE SAME AS GLUTEN-FREE, and the gap matters: 十割 describes the DOUGH, not the process. Boards are dusted with 打ち粉 to stop the noodles sticking, and 打ち粉 is usually wheat flour; the noodles are boiled in water shared with everything else the kitchen cooks; and this shop also serves tempura, which puts wheat batter in the same room. The shop makes no gluten-free claim and publishes no allergen information. Worth a phone call about the 打ち粉 specifically — if it is buckwheat or potato starch, this becomes one of the most interesting soba records in the dataset.
